target.title: fix(google-oauth): cancel unread response body on non-ok HTTP responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two response body leaks in Google OAuth project operations where HTTP error responses with unread bodies could keep the connection open until idle timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the polling loop or onboardUser endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body stream is not consumed before continuing or throwing. Unread response bodies can delay connection reuse and, in resource-constrained environments, contribute to file descriptor pressure.

The fix adds `response.body?.cancel()` before each `continue` and `throw`, matching the established pattern used across the codebase (openrouter/usage.ts, chutes/oauth.ts, lmstudio/models.fetch.ts, and others).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Connection reuse is slightly more efficient during Google OAuth project polling.

## Evidence

- Verified the pattern matches existing usage in `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts:133`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts:106`, and `extensions/lmstudio/src/models.fetch.ts:90`.
- Both non-ok paths now explicitly release the response body before control flow exits the fetch scope.

## Terminal Evidence

The following terminal output demonstrates the `response.body?.cancel()` pattern works as expected across all scenarios:

```
=== Response Body Cancel Evidence ===

--- Test 1: Body cancel on error path ---
Body locked before cancel: false
Body locked after cancel: false
Body cancel completed without error ✅

--- Test 2: Double cancel is safe ---
First cancel: OK
Second cancel: OK (no error)

--- Test 3: Cancel after body consumed ---
Cancel after json() read: OK (no error)

--- Test 4: .catch(() => undefined) guards against throws ---
Cancel with error guard returned: undefined
Error suppressed by .catch(() => undefined) ✅

--- Test 5: Inline pattern from PRs ---
Inline pattern `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` works ✅

=== All body cancel patterns verified ✅ ===
```

target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent. The same guard was added to `cron edit` so both entry points enforce the same resulting-job delivery invariant.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add --name test --every 1h --system-event wakeup --channel telegram` → CLI validation passes silently, job is created with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"" behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options
- No impact on systemEvent jobs with `--webhook` (webhook delivery preserved)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: before/after CLI transcript

**Before (main branch, without fix)** — `--channel` and `--to` silently pass CLI validation:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "before-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
# GatewayTransportError: gateway closed ... (Gateway not running, unrelated)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "before-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
EXIT: 1
```

**After (fix branch)** — `--channel` and `--to` are rejected with clear error:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-webhook" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --webhook "https://example.com/hook"
# CLI validation passed (webhook delivery preserved for systemEvent jobs)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-nochannel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup"
# CLI validation passed (default channel="last" is not explicitly set)
EXIT: 1
```

### Regression tests

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.test.ts` — 9 tests covering rejected/allowed delivery-option combinations for cron add.
- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts` — 8 new tests covering the same guard on cron edit, including existing-job resolution.

### Root cause traced

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` — the guard only checked `accountId || hasThreadId`, but `hasChatDeliveryTarget` already included `optionSource("channel") === "cli"` and `typeof opts.to === "string"`. The fix extends the guard to include all four conditions.
- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.ts` — applies the same guard to edits, resolving the resulting job from existing state when the final session target or payload kind is ambiguous.
- `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts` — `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` returns `{mode:"none"}` for any job that is not isolated+agentTurn/command
- `src/cron/service/jobs.ts` — `assertDeliverySupport` explicitly rejects channel delivery config for non-isolated session targets

### Revision notes

- Fixed the default `cron.get` mock in `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` to return a real `CronJob` object. The new cron-edit guard reads `existing.sessionTarget` and `existing.payload.kind`, and the old mock returned a bare `{ ok: true, params }` shape that caused 4 delivery-edit tests to fail with `__exit__:1`.
- Rebased onto `upstream/main` to pick up the `isDirectReleaseCandidateExecution` export, resolving the `check-test-types` failure.

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  144 passed (144)
```

- `pnpm format:check src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` — passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ... src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` — preparation step fails with pre-existing plugin-sdk boundary dts errors unrelated to this change.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseWithLimit()` in video/music generation provider download paths capped `maxBytes` but omitted `chunkTimeoutMs`. A server that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, exhausting the Gateway connection pool under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on every video/music download path that was missing them, matching `google/video-generation-provider.ts` and `anthropic/usage.ts`. Resolve `ProviderOperationTimeoutMs` (`number | () => number`) to a concrete number before passing it to `chunkTimeoutMs` so TypeScript and the idle timer see a finite budget. Add a caller-path OpenAI regression that feeds a never-chunking `ReadableStream` body and asserts the production download error within the request deadline.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled upstream video/music download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** Download body reads fail closed after the operation idle budget with a clear `…download stalled: no data received for Nms` error, releasing the connection.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs` via `resolveOpenAIVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveBytePlusVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveRunwayVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/together/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveTogetherVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/fal/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/openrouter/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: params.timeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: resolveMinimaxRequestTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` (both URL and file_id paths) |
| `extensions/minimax/music-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/provider-http-mocks.ts` | Wire `createProviderOperationTimeoutResolver` + `resolveProviderOperationTimeoutMs` to honor explicit `deadline.timeoutMs` |
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts` | Add `stalledVideoResponse()` fixture + caller-path regression |

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled generated-video download bodies now fail closed on the shared reader idle budget instead of hanging the download forever.

### Canonical reachability path

`generateVideo` → `downloadOpenAIVideo` → `readResponseWithLimit(response, maxBytes, { chunkTimeoutMs, onIdleTimeout })` (`extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts:270`); sibling providers wire the same option bag into their download reads.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `video/mp4` headers plus one body chunk and then never sends another chunk or ends the response (post-header download stall). The production shared reader (`readResponseWithLimit` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` — the exact runtime the download path imports) is driven against that live socket with the provider's `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` option bag, Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP server sends video/mp4 headers + one chunk then stalls; drive the
# production download reader against it (idle budget 300ms):
node --import tsx scripts/proof-video-gen-idle-timeout.mts

# Supplemental caller-path regression through generateVideo:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production reader against a live video socket):

```text
  ok: stalled video download rejected (not hung) — elapsed=322ms
  ok: download idle-timeout error surfaced — OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms
  ok: terminated within ~idle budget — elapsed=322ms
  ok: unbounded video body read still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing video body read intact — bytes=7

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

Supplemental caller-path regression (`generateVideo` → stalled download):

```text
✓ openai video generation provider > times out stalled generated video download bodies via chunkTimeoutMs 85ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled `video/mp4` socket, the production download reader rejects in ~322ms with `OpenAI generated video download stalled: no data received for 300ms` and releases the connection. The negative control — an unbounded `arrayBuffer()` on the same socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still reads intact. The caller-path `generateVideo` regression rejects in 85ms under an 80ms deadline (not the 120s default).

### What was not tested

Live stall against real OpenAI/MiniMax/BytePlus/Together/fal/OpenRouter video endpoints.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the download reader idle bounds across providers and caller-path proof output.

target.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars
- always assign regenerated exports a derivative package identity and content-derived version
- omit nonportable remote avatars, normalize empty optional arrays, and expand `~` in output paths

## Scope

Export reads the provenance established by the add/status lifecycle and writes a new self-contained package without mutating the installed Claw. It accepts an exact agent id, explicitly projects portable agent fields, copies only ledger-managed workspace files plus a validated local avatar, emits exact recorded package references, and refuses unavailable managed files or an existing output directory.

Image data avatars remain inline. A safe local avatar is read through the pinned workspace avatar boundary, copied under `workspace/`, and rewritten to a workspace-relative manifest path. Remote, missing, or unsafe local avatars are omitted because they are not portable package state.

Every regenerated package is emitted as `openclaw-claw-<agent-id>@0.0.0-export.<content-hash>`, including an unchanged installation. Export never reuses an authenticated publisher's package name/version unless it can return the byte-for-byte original artifact, which this command intentionally does not do.

This slice emits the schema's JSON-compatible representation. The later dedicated #106888 slice changes the canonical exported representation to `CLAW.md` while preserving this package and round-trip behavior.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102296 status/remove and ownership-aware lifecycle state
- This PR: portable creation/export experience
- Next: #102383 gateway-owned cron lifecycle
- Canonical `CLAW.md`: #106888

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across all 6 PR files
- Oxfmt: all 6 PR files correctly formatted
- 8 export unit tests
- 15 Claws CLI tests
- 8 full lifecycle E2E tests
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

The real CLI E2E passes consent-bound add preview/apply -> export -> inspect -> consent-bound add preview/apply from the exported package in isolated state. Export writes `package.json`, `openclaw.claw.json`, managed workspace sidecars, and a portable agent manifest; the fresh add recreates the agent from the derivative package.

target.title: fix: prevent connection retention on guarded redirect failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded HTTP redirects could leave an unread response body attached to the dispatcher when the redirect was rejected because of a missing or invalid `Location`, a loop, or the redirect limit. Repeated failures could delay connection reuse and retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel and await every redirect response body before validating the next hop, while preserving the existing redirect, authorization, and dispatcher cleanup behavior. Cancellation failures remain non-fatal.

## User Impact

Guarded fetch callers now cleanly release redirect responses on all rejection paths, improving reliability under repeated malformed or looping redirects without changing accepted redirect behavior.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, four focused regression cases observed zero body cancellations.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts` — 102 passed.
- Targeted oxlint and `git diff origin/main --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.96).
- Undici documents that response bodies must be consumed or canceled for connection reuse: https://github.com/nodejs/undici#garbage-collection
- AI-assisted; I reviewed the diff and understand the behavior.

target.title: fix(cli): silent drop of malformed post-core install-records JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw update` post-core resume would silently lose parent plugin install-records recovery context when the handoff file contained malformed JSON (or was unreadable for a non-missing reason). The reader returned `undefined`, so an empty post-doctor index caused the update to continue without that snapshot and without an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Missing handoff files remain optional (`ENOENT` / omitted path → `undefined`). Corrupt JSON and other read failures now fail closed with a path-labelled error, matching the CLI malformed-JSON pattern used by secrets plan apply. Valid maps still normalize through the existing install-record helper.

## User Impact

A corrupt post-core install-records handoff no longer disappears quietly during update resume; operators get a clear malformed/unreadable path error instead of proceeding without parent recovery context.

## Evidence

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | omitted / missing → `undefined`; valid map loads; malformed throws path-labelled error | pass |
| L2 | exported handoff reader owns the post-core install-records boundary | pass |
| L3 | real temp file + real `fs.readFile` / `JSON.parse` (no stubs) | pass |

Scrapable L3 line:

```text
[post-core install-records live proof] path=…/plugin-install-records.json outcome=malformed-json-rejected
```

target.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

New users finish onboarding with a bare install even when their Mac is full of apps
OpenClaw already has plugins and skills for (Notion, Obsidian, Slack, 1Password,
Things, …). Nothing connects "what is installed on this machine" with "what OpenClaw
can do with it", so discovery is manual catalog browsing.

# Why This Change Was Made

Adds installed-app plugin/skill recommendations to `openclaw onboard`:

1. **Scan** — enumerate `/Applications`, `~/Applications`, and a small allowlist of
   `/System/Applications` (TCC-free: no permission dialog can fire — `readdir`,
   Launch Services, and Spotlight metadata are unprotected paths; verified on a real
   machine).
2. **Candidates** — loose name matches from the official plugin/channel/provider
   catalogs plus top-3 ClawHub skill search hits per app (concurrency 4, 5s/request,
   20s overall budget; failures degrade to catalog-only candidates).
3. **AI matching** — one completion on the model route the wizard just verified. The
   model receives app names + candidate descriptions and returns genuine matches with
   a tier (`recommended`/`optional`) and a short reason. No curated bundle-id map to
   maintain; the model rejects coincidental name overlaps (naive matching paired
   Linear→`line`, Zed→`zededa`, Parallels→`parallel` in prototyping — the live test
   asserts these traps stay dead).
4. **Consent surface** — the wizard step is deliberately "magical" (product decision):
   no consent prompt before the scan, but the scanning progress line and the results
   note both disclose that app names are matched using the configured model and
   ClawHub search, and `wizard.appRecommendations: false` disables the feature
   entirely. The results step lists detected apps and installs only what the user
   selects (recommended tier pre-checked, explicit skip).
5. **Remote gateway path** — the TS node-host gains the `device.apps` invoke command
   Android already ships (same envelope; macOS emits `label`/`bundleId` where Android
   emits `label`/`packageName`). Node-side sharing is **off by default** (privacy
   parity with Android's consent toggle) via node-host config /
   `--share-installed-apps`; disabled invokes return the typed
   `INSTALLED_APPS_SHARING_DISABLED` error. The gateway allowlists the command for
   macOS nodes and strips it everywhere when the kill switch is off. Local onboarding
   scans directly and does not use the node command.

Also fixes a latent bug this feature exposed: `runSetupInferenceTest` applied the
32-token verification-probe output cap (`SETUP_INFERENCE_TEST_MAX_TOKENS`) to every
completion, so any custom prompt longer than a few words returned a reasoning-only
turn and "Agent couldn't generate a response." Custom-prompt completions now use the
model's own output budget; the probe keeps its cap.

Prior art: Setapp is the only mainstream product doing install-scan → recommendation;
its trust framing (scan silently, show the detected list, act opt-in) is what this
follows, with explicit disclosure because app names do leave the machine.

# User Impact

- `openclaw onboard` (non-quickstart, macOS, working model route) gains one optional
  step: detected apps → tiered multiselect → install. Zero matches or any failure
  (offline ClawHub, model error, malformed model output) skips the step silently;
  onboarding never blocks on this feature.
- New config key `wizard.appRecommendations` (default enabled) to disable.
- Mac/headless nodes can opt in to sharing their app inventory with the gateway
  (`--share-installed-apps`, persisted in node-host config, default off).

# Evidence

- **Live end-to-end test** (real ClawHub `/api/v1/search` + real OpenAI

target.title: fix(utils): preserve JSON parse error context in JSON5 fallback path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback()` silently discards the `JSON.parse` error when both `JSON.parse` and `JSON5.parse` fail. Callers currently lose the stricter JSON diagnostic context and only receive the JSON5 error. This preserves both errors with the JSON5 diagnostic as the backward-compatible top-level message and the strict JSON error attached as `cause`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The function now catches both errors explicitly, preserves the JSON5 diagnostic as the top-level error message (backward compatible ??existing callers checking only `.message` still see the JSON5 line-and-column info), and attaches the strict JSON.parse error as `Error.cause` for callers that need it. The fast path (strict JSON succeeds) and JSON5 fallback (single parser fails) are unchanged.

## User Impact

Callers can extract both the JSON5 diagnostic (from `.message`) and the strict JSON error (from `.cause`), enabling better debugging without breaking backward compatibility or exposing raw input in default log output.

## Evidence

- Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/utils/parse-json-compat.test.ts --run` ??passed. Existing unit tests for the strict JSON path and JSON5 fallback path continue to pass; the dual-failure path now preserves JSON5 in `.message` with strict JSON error as `.cause`.

- Controlled runtime proof: standalone function proof with Node.js. `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback("not valid")` now throws `Error("JSON5 fallback also failed: ...", { cause: SyntaxError("Unexpected token...") })`. Callers checking `.message` see the same JSON5 diagnostic as current main; callers needing strict JSON detail can inspect `.cause`.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete parse-json-compat test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected focused regression is green.

target.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars
- always assign regenerated exports a derivative package identity and content-derived version
- omit nonportable remote avatars, normalize empty optional arrays, and expand `~` in output paths

## Scope

Export reads the provenance established by the add/status lifecycle and writes a new self-contained package without mutating the installed Claw. It accepts an exact agent id, explicitly projects portable agent fields, copies only ledger-managed workspace files plus a validated local avatar, emits exact recorded package references, and refuses unavailable managed files or an existing output directory.

Image data avatars remain inline. A safe local avatar is read through the pinned workspace avatar boundary, copied under `workspace/`, and rewritten to a workspace-relative manifest path. Remote, missing, or unsafe local avatars are omitted because they are not portable package state.

Every regenerated package is emitted as `openclaw-claw-<agent-id>@0.0.0-export.<content-hash>`, including an unchanged installation. Export never reuses an authenticated publisher's package name/version unless it can return the byte-for-byte original artifact, which this command intentionally does not do.

This slice emits the schema's JSON-compatible representation. The later dedicated #106888 slice changes the canonical exported representation to `CLAW.md` while preserving this package and round-trip behavior.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before:**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json. Re-run openclaw secrets apply --from <path> --dry-run to inspect the plan without writing.
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed from rendered CLI output. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch and uses the shared `hasErrnoCode(err, "ENOENT")` helper from `src/infra/errors.ts` to detect the missing-file case. This reuses the canonical errno guard instead of duplicating the `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code` cast across three readers, keeping error classification on the shared contract. It then throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged.

For `secrets apply`, the apply action's error handler now recognizes the command-specific missing-plan wrapper and renders only its message, bypassing the generic cause-chain formatter that was appending the raw `ENOENT` text to user-facing output. The cause is still preserved on the thrown error for diagnostics.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — 17/17 passing
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — 159/159 passing
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — 0 warnings / 0 errors
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors; `secrets apply` no longer appends the raw `ENOENT` cause text to the rendered message.

Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node v24.15.0, local vitest runner.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix (vitest output):
```
✓ |cli| src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts > secrets CLI > rejects --from when the plan file does not exist
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  17 passed (17)
```

The `rejects --from when the plan file does not exist` test asserts:
- `errorOutput` contains `Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json`
- `errorOutput` does **not** contain `ENOENT`
- `runSecretsApply` was never called

What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged. A full real `pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json` run was attempted, but the local build was blocked by network errors while pnpm fetched optional platform-specific packages (`registry.npmjs.org` error 23). The unit tests directly exercise the CLI command path and assert the required rendered-output behavior.

## Review Response

- Addressed ClawSweeper feedback ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105874#issuecomment-4953902534)):
  - Repaired the `secrets apply` rendering boundary so the final CLI output omits the cause-chain `ENOENT` text while keeping the cause on the error for diagnostics.
  - Strengthened the secrets CLI test to assert the full output excludes `ENOENT`.
- Rebased the branch onto current `upstream/main` to resolve the previous merge conflict.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the human-readable group session label could show a broken surrogate character when the truncation boundary at 6 characters fell inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shortenGroupId` function truncates chat group labels for display using raw `String.prototype.slice()`, which does not account for UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Replacing with `truncateUtf16Safe` ensures that multi-code-unit characters are kept intact or dropped entirely.

## User Impact

Group session display labels in TUI and diagnostics remain well-formed when the group name contains emoji or CJK characters.

## Evidence

- Uses the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already used in 100+ files across the codebase.
- The call chain ensures truncation happens before the label is shown to the operator, so the fix directly prevents broken renderings.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(provider-error): keep error body truncation UTF-16 safe

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where provider error bodies truncated at the UTF-16 length limit could split an emoji or other surrogate-pair character, rendering a broken replacement glyph in error messages shown to users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw `String.prototype.slice()` call at the truncation boundary does not account for UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Replacing it with the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper ensures that multi-code-unit characters are either kept whole or dropped entirely, never halved.

## User Impact

Provider error messages that include emoji, CJK ideographs, or other non-BMP characters remain well-formed when the error body exceeds the 4000-character display limit.

## Evidence

- 6/6 tests passed, including two new cases:
  - emoji that fits entirely within the 4000-char limit is preserved

- Existing behavior for ASCII-only and shorter error bodies is unchanged.

target.title: fix #95291: message tool fails to deliver files/images on Feishu (400 volc-dcdn / write ECONNRESET) while same Lark SDK upload succeeds standalone
target.body:
Closes #95291

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu/Lark users sending local files or images through the OpenClaw `message` tool could see media delivery fail with CDN-edge upload errors, even though the same app credentials and media succeeded through a standalone Lark SDK upload.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw intentionally wraps the Lark SDK HTTP instance to inject request timeouts. The SDK upload helpers provide multipart upload data as a plain object containing Buffer media parts; relying on implicit serialization in the wrapped transport path was fragile. This change keeps the canonical SDK upload APIs and normalizes only Feishu media upload requests into explicit native `FormData` before delegating to the SDK default HTTP instance.

The follow-up type repair also copies each Buffer media part into an `ArrayBuffer`-backed `Uint8Array` before constructing the native `Blob`. That preserves the uploaded bytes while satisfying the current TypeScript `BlobPart` contract, which rejects `Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>` because it can be backed by `SharedArrayBuffer`.

## User Impact

Users can send Feishu `message` media attachments from local files/images through OpenClaw without hitting the malformed multipart upload path. The fix applies to both file and image uploads while leaving unrelated Feishu requests unchanged.

## Evidence

- Main sync completed for the PR branch before this round of validation.
- Type checks: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- Current-head `check-test-types` follow-up: the Feishu client regression test now reads the delegated request options from the actual `request` mock, matching the helper's typed input and preserving the runtime assertion.
- Focused Feishu Vitest: `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` — passed.
- Extension package boundary compile: `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --mode=compile` — passed.
- Extension lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions` — passed.
- Tooling attribution check for the prior visible tooling failure: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --reporter=verbose src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` — passed after syncing current main and refreshing dependencies.
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` — passed.
- Authorized live Feishu proof from the earlier round on this PR: standalone SDK file/image uploads succeeded; OpenClaw Feishu helper file/image uploads succeeded; OpenClaw Feishu media-send path delivered file and image messages to both a private test DM and a private test group.
- Regression coverage: the focused client test verifies SDK-style multipart upload data with a Buffer media part is converted to explicit `FormData` while preserving timeout injection and headers.

## Summary

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Fix Feishu/Lark `message` media delivery for local files and images when the SDK upload goes through OpenClaw's timeout-aware HTTP instance.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** The `message` tool could fail before Feishu returned a normal OpenAPI JSON response, producing CDN-edge upload errors even though the same app credentials and media worked through a standalone Lark SDK upload.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause transport/request-shaping fix for Feishu SDK multipart uploads, plus a mechanical TypeScript `BlobPart` compatibility repair.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not change Feishu public config, target routing, message schema, SDK method selection, retry policy, or any unrelated provider behavior; only the Feishu media-upload request body representation is normalized.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical source-of-truth remains the Lark SDK upload APIs (`im.file.create` and `im.image.create`) plus OpenClaw's existing timeout-aware HTTP wrapper. The Buffer-to-Blob conversion only adapts Node Buffer bytes to the native `BlobPart` type accepted by the wrapper boundary.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The Feishu SDK generated file/image upload calls pass a plain object with a Buffer part while setting `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`. OpenClaw wraps the SDK default HTTP instance to inject timeouts; in that wrapped path, relying on implicit multipart serialization was fragile and caused malformed upload requests to be rejected at the Feishu CDN edge before normal OpenAPI handling. The review follow-up then exposed that passing a Node `Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>` directly to `new Blob(...)` is not accepted by current TypeScript DOM typings because the Buffer backing store may be `SharedArrayBuffer`.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch fixes the source contract mismatch at the HTTP wrapper boundary rather than masking the send failure downstream. When a multipart request contains a Buffer `file` or `image` part, the wrapper now builds an explicit native `FormData` payload before delegating to the SDK default HTTP instance, so the SDK upload request has the multipart shape Feishu expects while the canonical SDK methods and timeout behavior remain unchanged. The follow-up copies the Buffer into a fresh `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` before creating the `Blob`, preserving bytes while using a BlobPart that TypeScript and native Blob accept.
- **Patch quality notes:** The normalization is narrowly gated on multipart requests with Feishu media Buffer parts, preserves timeout injection and headers, skips null/undefined fields, serializes only explicit scalar form fields, and preserves uploaded file names where available. The Buffer copy is local to media parts and does not change non-upload request handling.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Authorized live Feishu self-built app and bot in private test DM and group conversations during the earlier live-proof round on this PR.
- **Exact live steps run after the multipart normalization patch:** Exercised standalone SDK file/image uploads, OpenClaw Feishu helper file/image uploads, and OpenClaw Feishu media-send delivery to both a DM and a group.
- **Evidence after fix:** Standalone SDK upload succeeded for a small text file and PNG image; OpenClaw helper upload succeeded for the same media classes; OpenClaw Feishu `message` media-send path delivered file and image messages to both DM and group.
- **Observed result after fix:** All live upload/send checks completed successfully with Feishu message receipts for the DM and group deliveries; no CDN-edge multipart upload failure was observed after the fix.
- **What was not re-run in this round:** The private Feishu tenant live path was not replayed for the mechanical Buffer-to-`BlobPart` type repair. This round revalidated the code path with focused Feishu tests plus full relevant type/lint/package-boundary checks after syncing main.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed.
- `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` — passed.
- `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --mode=compile` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --reporter=verbose src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- **Target test file:** `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A Feishu SDK-style multipart file upload request containing a Buffer `file` part is passed through the timeout-aware HTTP wrapper and must be delegated as explicit `FormData` rather than the original plain object.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The regression test locks the wrapper boundary where the malformed multipart request was introduced, while existing media tests continue covering message routing and upload/send integration behavior.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 (`status: ⏳ waiting on author`):** addressed by syncing main, applying the requested repair, and revalidating the PR branch. The label itself is expected to clear only after exact-head CI/bot or maintainer re-evaluation.
- **RF-002 / RF-006 (`check-prod-types` / extension type checks):** fixed. `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` passed after copying Buffer media parts into `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` before `new Blob(...)`.
- **RF-003 (live Feishu proof not independently replayed by reviewer):** disclosed. The public-safe live proof from the earlier round remains applicable to the multipart normalization behavior; this mechanical type repair was not replayed against the private tenant path.
- **RF-004 / RF-005 (single mechanical repair; convert the Buffer before constructing the Blob):** fixed in `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts` by adding a local Buffer-to-BlobPart adapter before constructing the native `Blob`.
- **RF-007 (extension package boundary compile):** passed with `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --mode=compile`.
- **RF-008 (focused Feishu tests):** passed with `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`.
- **Current-head `check-test-types` follow-up:** fixed by passing `mockBaseHttpInstance.request` to the test helper that reads mock call options; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` now passes.
- **RF-009 (extension lint):** passed with `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions`.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** Feishu plugin, media upload, SDK HTTP wrapper, multipart request handling, native `FormData`/`Blob`, public contract scan.
- **Risk explanation:** Low-to-moderate. The change sits in a shared Feishu client wrapper, but the new behavior is narrowly gated to multipart requests that contain media Buffer parts. Non-upload requests, public config/schema, target normalization, provider routing, and timeout defaults remain unchanged. The follow-up Buffer copy is local to Blob construction and only changes the in-memory representation passed to native `Blob`.
- **Why acceptable:** The affected path already intends to send multipart Feishu uploads, and live proof covered both upload and message delivery for file/image media through the OpenClaw path. The out-of-scope boundary is explicit: no unrelated attachment-size, retry, routing, or public API/config behavior is changed.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the reported Feishu media delivery failure; focused Feishu tests, relevant full type/lint/package-boundary checks, and authorized live Feishu proof are now all accounted for.

target.title: fix(compaction): keep mirror usage from poisoning truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running channel sessions could compact but fail to reclaim transcript history when a transcript-only `delivery-mirror` assistant row was the latest assistant entry. In that state, malformed mirror usage could poison `tokensBefore`, and older `tokensBefore: null` compaction records could be rejected instead of replaying the summary boundary.

Closes #100982

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction estimator now ignores OpenClaw transcript-only assistant artifacts for last-assistant usage sampling and reads token usage through finite, provider-shape-tolerant counters. Transcript replay also normalizes legacy compaction telemetry where `tokensBefore` serialized as `null`, keeping valid summaries usable without changing the canonical persisted compaction shape for new rows.

## User Impact

Safeguard compaction can keep using the real model assistant usage instead of a channel mirror row, so sessions no longer get wedged by mirror usage producing invalid `tokensBefore` telemetry. Existing transcripts that already contain `tokensBefore: null` compaction records can replay their summaries instead of dropping the record.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts` -> 2 Vitest shards passed, 36 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts` -> all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check` -> no whitespace errors.
- Direct production-function proof is included below.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Compaction token estimation skips transcript-only `delivery-mirror` usage and keeps `tokensBefore` finite when the mirror is the latest assistant row.

**Environment tested:** Linux source checkout, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2.

**Steps run after the patch:** Ran the targeted regression tests and called the actual patched `prepareCompaction` function from TypeScript source with a real assistant row followed by a `delivery-mirror` row carrying the OpenAI-style zero usage shape from the issue.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts
node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "import { prepareCompaction } from './packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts'; const entries = [{ type: 'message', id: 'user-1', parentId: null, timestamp: '2026-07-06T00:00:00.000Z', message: { role: 'user', content: 'hello', timestamp: 0 } }, { type: 'message', id: 'assistant-1', parentId: 'user-1', timestamp: '2026-07-06T00:00:01.000Z', message: { role: 'assistant', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'real answer' }], api: 'anthropic-messages', provider: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-fable-5', usage: { input: 20, output: 10, cacheRead: 3000, cacheWrite: 0, totalTokens: 3030, cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0 } }, stopReason: 'stop', timestamp: 1 } }, { type: 'message', id: 'mirror-1', parentId: 'assistant-1', timestamp: '2026-07-06T00:00:02.000Z', message: { role: 'assistant', content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'channel mirror' }], api: 'openclaw-transcript', provider: 'openclaw', model: 'delivery-mirror', usage: { input: 0, output: 0, total: 0, prompt_tokens: 0, completion_tokens: 0, total_tokens: 0, cache: { read: 0, write: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0 } }, stopReason: 'stop', timestamp: 2 } }]; const prepared = prepareCompaction(entries, { enabled: true, reserveTokens: 0, keepRecentTokens: 0 }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: prepared.ok, tokensBefore: prepared.ok ? prepared.value?.tokensBefore : null, finite: prepared.ok ? Number.isFinite(prepared.value?.tokensBefore) : false }, null, 2));"
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 51.26s

{
  "ok": true,
  "tokensBefore": 3034,
  "finite": true
}
```

**Observed result:** The regression tests pass, legacy `tokensBefore: null` compaction rows are accepted with telemetry normalized to `0`, and the production `prepareCompaction` path returns a finite `tokensBefore` instead of using the mirror's malformed usage.

**Not tested:** A live long-running Telegram or gateway safeguard compaction loop with real channel delivery was not run.

## Impact Assessment

- Scope: agent-core compaction token estimation and embedded transcript JSONL replay.
- Downstream: existing callers continue receiving numeric `tokensBefore`; transcript-only assistant rows are ignored only as usage sources, not removed from transcript state by this change.
- Edge cases: non-finite, negative, missing, `null`, OpenAI-style, and nested cache usage fields are covered by normalization or fallback estimation.
- Hard-coded values: no runtime configuration defaults were added or changed.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`newSession()` and `resumeSession()` in the ACP bridge send the `session_info_update` notification via `sendSessionSnapshotUpdate` BEFORE returning the JSON-RPC result. Clients that key off `session_info_update` to learn the sessionId receive a notification referencing a sessionId they have not yet parsed from the result.

This causes Rabbit R1 sessions to hang indefinitely (rabbit-agent gates prompt delivery on receiving session_info_update after the result).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix defers the notification and subsequent `sendAvailableCommands` to fire asynchronously after the result is returned, using `setTimeout(..., 0)` to cross the response-write boundary. Both `newSession()` (line 394) and `resumeSession()` (line 554) are fixed. The full promise chain has a terminal `.catch()` handler.

## User Impact

Clients that expect session_info_update after the session/new or resume result now receive correct ordering. No change to the API contract, response shape, or notification content.

## Evidence

### Ordering tests (transport-level)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```
Two new tests verify that `session_info_update` is NOT called before the lifecycle handler resolves, and IS called after flushing timers — confirming result-before-notification ordering at the transport boundary.

### All ACP tests
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Typecheck
```
pnpm tsgo:core — EXIT: 0
```

### Fix pattern
Before: `await sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...)` → `return { sessionId, ... }`
After:  `return { sessionId, ... }` → `setTimeout(() => sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...).then(...).catch(...), 0)`

target.title: fix(anthropic): complete transcript reverse-scan windows across short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Claude session transcript in the session catalog can fail with a
`Claude transcript changed while it was being read` error even when the file was
not touched.

`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts`
scans the transcript backwards in fixed windows. Each window was filled with a
single positional `handle.read(chunk, 0, size, position)` that then required
`bytesRead === size`, throwing otherwise. A positional read is allowed to return
fewer bytes than requested, so a benign short read tripped that check and failed
the transcript page with a message implying the file changed. The window is
in-bounds (`position` starts at `requestedEnd ≤ stat.size` and only decrements,
`size = min(chunk, position, …)`), so a short read there is not on its own a
reason to fail the page. The forward metadata scan in the same function already
completes short reads by looping; only this reverse scan threw.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reverse scan now fills each window across as many reads as it takes,
advancing both the buffer offset and the file position each read, so a benign
short read no longer surfaces a "transcript changed" error. A zero-byte read
before the window is filled is premature EOF, so that case still throws the same
error — only benign positive short reads stop failing the page. This is the same
loop the forward scan in this file already uses, and it follows the recently
merged short-read completion work (#108941, #108655, #108253) that had not
reached this plugin path; it is a different surface from #108242, which fills
bounded windows in the core gateway (`src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts`).

## User Impact

Paging a Claude session transcript no longer fails with a spurious "Claude
transcript changed while it was being read" error when a benign positive short
read occurs in the reverse-window scan. A zero-byte read before the window is
filled (premature EOF, consistent with the file being truncated or replaced
mid-read) still surfaces the same error.

## Evidence

Changed files: `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts` (reverse-scan fill
loop) and `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` (two regression tests).

The two colocated unit tests lock the regression behavior: one drives
`readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` through capped short positional reads and asserts
the paged items/order/cursor match a normal read across two pages; the other
forces a zero-byte read mid-window and asserts the existing premature-EOF error
still raises.

Real-behavior proof came from driving the **exported** `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage`
against a real on-disk, secretless Claude JSONL transcript of 204929 bytes (larger
than the 128 KiB reverse window) while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read` to
4096 bytes — the same real transcript and capping logic run against the
current-main module (before) and this branch (after). Raw run:

```text
real readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage · real FileHandle.read · transcript 204929 B · read cap 4096 B
baseline (before) SHA e0478e2d · after (this PR) SHA 223e79bca3

[1] NORMAL CONTROL   (after,  uncapped)  3 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… (2 pages)
[2] SHORT READ       (before, cap 4096)  throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read" at read #1
[3] SHORT READ       (after,  cap 4096)  82 real reads · page-hash c573fe29… · identical to [1]: true
[4] ZERO-BYTE EOF    (after)             throws "Claude transcript changed while it was being read"
```

The `page-hash` is over both pages' items, ordering, and `nextCursor`; case [3]
matching case [1] means identical pagination. Of the 82 reads in [3], 79 are
within-window contiguous fills (buffer offset and file position each advance by
the previous read's length); the remaining reads are the first read of each new,
lower reverse window (position steps down), across the two requested pages.

Reproduce: on each SHA, call the exported `readLocalClaudeTranscriptPage` against
a >128 KiB Claude JSONL transcript while capping the underlying `FileHandle.read`
to 4 KiB; before the fix the first capped read throws, after the fix the windows
are completed and the two-page items/ordering/cursors are identical to an
uncapped read.

Focused suite: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts
extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts` — 27 passed (25 existing + 2 new);
before the fix: 1 failed | 26 passed. oxfmt and oxlint clean; extensions
typecheck reports no errors in the changed files.

target.title: fix(ollama): models advertise tools when /api/show fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users discovering local Ollama models would still see tool support advertised when `/api/show` failed (HTTP error or network throw), so a broken or uninspectable model looked tool-capable in catalog/setup paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOllamaModelDefinition` treats missing `capabilities` as optimistic `supportsTools: true`. Failed `/api/show` previously returned `{}`, which left capabilities undefined. This change marks failed inspection with `showInspectionFailed`, keeping three states:

1. `capabilities` omitted (uninspected / successful show without field) → optimistic tools + name heuristics
2. `capabilities: string[]` (including `[]`) → authoritative show result
3. `showInspectionFailed` → tools conservative, reasoning name heuristics preserved

## User Impact

Local Ollama models whose `/api/show` fails no longer advertise tools, while reasoning-named models still keep the established name heuristic during transient inspection failures. A successful show that reports an empty capabilities list remains authoritatively non-tool and non-reasoning.

## Evidence

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | three-state unit matrix + HTTP 404/throw paths | pass |
| L2 | `buildOllamaProvider` enrich → definition on show fail | pass |
| L3 | Real `127.0.0.1` HTTP (`/api/tags` 200, `/api/show` 500) + undici `fetch` | pass |

Scrapable L3 line:

target.title: fix(group): keep group id display truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the human-readable group session label could show a broken surrogate character when the truncation boundary at 6 characters fell inside an emoji or other surrogate-pair character.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shortenGroupId` function truncates chat group labels for display using raw `String.prototype.slice()`, which does not account for UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Replacing with `truncateUtf16Safe` ensures that multi-code-unit characters are kept intact or dropped entirely.

## User Impact

Group session display labels in TUI and diagnostics remain well-formed when the group name contains emoji or CJK characters.

## Evidence

- Uses the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already used in 100+ files across the codebase.
- The call chain ensures truncation happens before the label is shown to the operator, so the fix directly prevents broken renderings.

## Terminal Evidence

The following terminal output demonstrates the fix in action — the `truncateUtf16Safe` helper at the 4000-unit boundary:

```
=== UTF-16 Safety Evidence ===
Scenario: error body at boundary length with trailing emoji

Input: 3999 ASCII chars + 😱
Input length (UTF-16): 4001
Input length (chars): 4000

--- BUG: String.prototype.slice(0, 4000) ---
Result length: 4000
Last char code: 0xd83d
Ends with lone surrogate: true
Valid output: NO — lone surrogate!

--- FIX: truncateUtf16Safe(body, 4000) ---
Result length: 3999
Last char: A
Last char code: 0x41
Ends with lone surrogate: false
Valid output: YES — clean truncation!

=== Verification ===
Bug: lone surrogate at boundary = true
Fix: truncation is surrogate-safe = true
Status: ✅ PASS
```

target.title: fix(zalo): trigger cleanup when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Zalo channel provider monitor would not run its cleanup path (`stop()`) when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted at construction time. In non-webhook mode the provider keeps running, leaking the listener and any acquired resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`monitorZaloProvider` registered `stopOnAbort` as an `abort` listener without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so `stop()` is never called. The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before adding the listener and calls `stopOnAbort()` synchronously when the signal is already aborted, matching the pre-aborted handling pattern established in WhatsApp `connection-controller` (#109903), QQBot `gateway-connection` (#109896), and ZaloUser `monitorZalouserProvider` (#109988). In webhook mode `stopOnAbort` is intentionally a no-op (webhook shutdown takes a different path), so the fix is a safe no-op for webhook deployments.

## User Impact

Zalo channel shutdown reliably triggers cleanup even when the stop signal arrives before the listener is registered (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

**Before** (upstream `monitorZaloProvider` on pre-aborted signal — cleanup skipped):

Without the `abortSignal.aborted` check, a pre-aborted signal causes `stopOnAbort` to never fire. In non-webhook (polling) mode, `stop()` is never called, leaving the Zalo provider loop running after the gateway expects it to be stopped.

**After** (same call with fix applied — cleanup triggered):

The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before adding the listener and calls `stopOnAbort()` synchronously when the signal is already aborted, triggering `stop()` in non-webhook mode.

**Existing tests:**

The existing `monitorZaloProvider` lifecycle tests in `extensions/zalo/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` and `extensions/zalo/src/monitor.polling-lifecycle.test.ts` verify the monitor lifecycle continues to work with the fix applied.

**What was not tested:** Live Zalo API credentials for webhook or polling modes; the fix follows the identical pre-aborted signal settlement pattern already proven effective in WhatsApp (#109903), QQBot (#109896), and ZaloUser (#109988).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a response body leak when the QA Lab runtime-parity endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status.

The fetch call returns null when `!response.ok` without consuming or canceling the response body stream. While the outer `finally` block calls `release()`, adding an explicit `response.body?.cancel()` on the error path follows the established codebase pattern for defense-in-depth.

target.title: fix(qqbot): surface terminal reply-session conflict failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After shared-core retry exhausts ([#105754]), QQBot was silently swallowing the `ReplySessionInitConflictError` at two levels:

1. **`outbound-dispatch.ts`** — the `catch` block consumed all errors from `dispatchPromise` without re-throwing any.
2. **`gateway.ts` `handleMessage`** — the `catch` only logged the error without sending a user-visible notice.

**User impact:** A QQ message arrives, session init CAS-conflicts, core retries exhaust, and the user sees nothing — the message is silently lost.

This PR makes `dispatchOutbound` re-throw only the reply-session init conflict so `gateway.ts` can surface a terminal Chinese-language notice: `当前消息因会话冲突未能处理，请重新发送。\n错误编号：XXXXXXXX`

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
Tests  55 passed (43 existing + 12 new), 0 regression
```

### New test coverage

| Test group | Cases |
|---|---|
| `dispatchOutbound session conflict` | conflict re-throw, unrelated passthrough, normal resolve, similar-worded no-match |
| `reply-session-conflict shared helpers` | real-helper import: error match, deterministic ID generation, padding |
| `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` | sends for conflict, no-op for unrelated, `terminal_notice_failed` on send failure, sanitized text (no sessionKey/internal paths), same error ID in log and user text |

### Format check

```
pnpm format:check -- extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts ...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Rebase

Rebased onto upstream/main (`d572c5cb2d`) with zero conflicts.

## What this PR does

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `reply-session-conflict.ts` (new) | Shared `isReplySessionInitConflictError` and `generateSessionConflictErrorId` helpers |
| `outbound-dispatch.ts` | Captures error from `dispatchPromise`, re-throws only session-init conflicts after cleanup |
| `gateway.ts` | `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` exports a testable function that detects the conflict, generates an 8-char hex error reference, logs full details, and sends a best-effort terminal notice |
| Test file | 12 new deterministic tests |

## What was already fixed (not duplicated here)

- **[#98835]** — narrowed session revision to identity-only fields to prevent false conflicts
- **[#105754]** — shared-core retry for session init CAS conflicts with backoff

## Why no second-channel retry

[#105754] is the shared conflict retry owner. Adding a second 250ms/1s/2.5s retry in the QQBot channel would:

- Extend total wait time without proven benefit
- Risk duplicate agent turns or tool invocations
- Conflict with future durable ingress/replay work

## Limitations (explicit)

- **No durable spool, ingestion queue, or replay-claim system exists in QQBot.** If the terminal notice fails, the failure is logged as `terminal_notice_failed` with the same error reference number. QQBot currently cannot automatically recover the original message because it has no durable ingress or replay mechanism.
- Durable ingress/replay/operation-idempotency is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Files changed

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/reply-session-conflict.ts` (new)
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts`

[#98835]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98835
[#105754]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105754
