target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's gateway already validates browser `Origin` on the WebSocket path, but only **post-handshake** (in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts`, after the socket is already open), and it does **not** defend against:

- **Header-smuggling / contradiction attacks** — a client forging `X-Forwarded-For` to disagree with `Forwarded` (or vice-versa) to confuse the resolved client IP / trust decision.
- **Cross-site WebSocket initiations (CSRF / DNS-rebinding class)** — there is no `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate anywhere in `main` (`git grep` confirms zero `sec-fetch-site` enforcement in `src/`).
- **Proto contradiction** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Forwarded proto` disagreeing with the actual socket transport (without breaking legitimate TLS-terminating trusted proxies).

These gaps are the WebSocket sibling of the HTTP ingress CSRF findings **#102834** (addressed on main) and **#96486**, and sit *under* the origin-allowlist work in **#98924** (which decides *which* origins pass, not *when/how the gate runs*).

This PR adds a self-contained **pre-handshake** `verifyClient` gate attached to the gateway `WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, so unauthenticated or forged clients never complete the HTTP 101 upgrade.

Pre-handshake is the only layer where the forwarded-header, proto-mismatch, and `Sec-Fetch-Site` signals can be evaluated — they are properties of the HTTP Upgrade request that post-handshake code never sees again.

**Distinct from adjacent items:** #102881 (merged) closed the HTTP `auth.mode=none` CSRF gap by adding `checkBrowserOrigin` to the HTTP auth path, post-routing. This PR is the WebSocket-upgrade sibling — it adds a pre-handshake `verifyClient` so header-only signals (forged forwarded headers, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, proto mismatch) can be rejected before the 101, on a surface #102881 does not touch. The existing post-handshake origin check in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts` remains unchanged and authoritative for role-scoped decisions (`isBrowserOperatorUi` / `isWebchat` / `isNativeAppUi`).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pre-handshake beats post-handshake.** Running the checks in `verifyClient` (before the 101) means a rejected client never gets a live socket, matching the defense-in-depth posture maintainers expect for a network-exposed gateway.
- **Reuses the shared `checkBrowserOrigin`** rather than reinventing origin logic, so allowlist / same-host / loopback behavior stays consistent with the HTTP/WS admission paths.
- **All strictness is opt-in and default-off** (`gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation`, `rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders`, `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests`), so existing deployments have **zero behavior change**. Non-browser clients (CLI, native apps) send no `Origin` and pass through; they authenticate post-handshake as today.
- **Trusted proxies are correctly exempted** from the proto-mismatch check — a TLS-terminating proxy legitimately presents plaintext to the gateway.

This is complementary to **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`): that PR extends *which* loopback origins are allowed; this PR adds the *enforcement layer* (pre-handshake gate, header contradiction, `Sec-Fetch-Site`). Neither duplicates the other.

## Prior Attempt & What Improved

This is a follow-up to my earlier (closed) PR **#35109** (`fix(gateway): surgical proxy-aware origin validation`), which edited the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` on the *post-handshake* WS path. Compared to that attempt, this PR:

- Moves the gate to **pre-handshake** (`verifyClient` before the 101) instead of extending the post-handshake check — a rejected client never opens a socket.
- Adds the **`Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site rejection** and **`X-Forwarded-For` vs `Forwarded` IP-contradiction** checks that #35109 did not cover.
- Keeps the change **self-contained** in `verify-client.ts` + `forwarded-headers.ts` rather than widening the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` contract used by every HTTP/WS caller.
- Ran the `autoreview` closeout gate before opening; it caught a real **`Origin: null` bypass** (a literal `null` origin was treated like an absent header and skipped all browser validation). Fixed in `verify-client.ts` with a regression test — the gate now only fast-passes on a *truly absent* Origin.

The goal was to take the earlier direction, make it architecturally cleaner, and actually vet it before asking for review.

## User Impact

- Network-exposed gateways gain a pre-handshake defense against forged forwarded headers and cross-site WebSocket CSRF, with **no config change required** for existing users (all new behavior opt-in).
- Operators who want stricter posture can enable:
  - `gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation` — reject duplicate / comma-chained sensitive proxy headers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders` — reject proxy headers from non-trusted peers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` — reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` / `cross-origin` WebSocket upgrades. **Off by default**; opt in only when every legitimate browser WS client is same-origin to the gateway. Loopback aliases (e.g. `localhost` -> `127.0.0.1`) are legitimately flagged cross-site by browsers, so the gate stays opt-in and `checkBrowserOrigin` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

### Real-behavior proof over a live WebSocket upgrade (head `1b5c1de`)

A real `node:http` server was bound on `127.0.0.1:18901` with a real
`ws.WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, verifyClient })`, wired through the actual
`createGatewayVerifyClient` from `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts`. Real HTTP
Upgrade requests were sent with browser/proxy headers and the observed status
line was recorded. This is not a mock — the wire path is the same path the
production gateway uses. Scenarios below were chosen to cover every case
ClawSweeper's prior review listed (browser, proxy, loopback-alias, native-client,
IPv4, IPv6).

```
== 1. native client (no Origin, no proxy headers) — non-browser pass-through ==
   request headers: {"host":"127.0.0.1:18901"}
   observed: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  ->  ACCEPTED

== 2. loopback-alias browser Origin (localhost -> 127.0.0.1, cross-site) ==
   [regression guard for v2026.4.15 / PR #66665 shipped contract]
   request headers: {"origin":"http://localhost:5173","host":"127.0.0.1:18901","sec-fetch-site":"cross-site"}
   observed: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  ->  ACCEPTED

== 3. allowed browser Origin (allowlist match) ==
   request headers: {"origin":"https://app.example.com","host":"127.0.0.1:18901"}
   observed: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  ->  ACCEPTED

== 4. disallowed browser Origin (not in allowlist) ==
   request headers: {"origin":"https://evil.example.com","host":"127.0.0.1:18901"}
   [verify-client] origin not allowed (origin not allowed)
   observed: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden  ->  REJECTED
   body: origin not allowed

== 5. cross-site WS rejection (Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site) with flag OPT-IN ==
   config gateway.security: {"rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests":true}
   request headers: {"origin":"https://app.example.com","host":"127.0.0.1:18901","sec-fetch-site":"cross-site"}
   [verify-client] cross-site websocket request rejected (sec-fetch-site=cross-site)
   observed: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden  ->  REJECTED
   body: cross-site request rejected

== 6. forwarded-header contradiction (X-Forwarded-For vs Forwarded, IPv6) ==
   [proves canonical IPv6 parsing — fixes split(":")[0] truncation finding]
   request headers: {"origin":"https://app.example.com","x-forwarded-for":"2001:db8::1","forwarded":"for=\"[2001:db8::dead:beef]\""}
   [verify-client] forwarded header inconsistency: X-Forwarded-For resolves to 2001:db8::1 but Forwarded resolves to 2001:db8::dead:beef
   observed: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request  ->  REJECTED
   body: invalid headers

== 7. forwarded-header AGREEMENT (matching IPv6 across forms: bracketed+port vs bracketed) ==
   [proves bracketed-with-port normalizes to bracketed IPv6; would have failed under old parser]
   request headers: {"x-forwarded-for":"[2001:db8::1]:12345","forwarded":"for=\"[2001:db8::1]\""}
   observed: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  ->  ACCEPTED

== 8. proto mismatch from UNTRUSTED peer (X-Forwarded-Proto: https on plaintext) ==
   request headers: {"x-forwarded-proto":"https"}  trustedProxies=[]
   [verify-client] origin protocol (http) does not match X-Forwarded-Proto (https)
   observed: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request  ->  REJECTED
   body: invalid protocol

== 9. proto mismatch from TRUSTED proxy (legitimate TLS-terminating proxy) ==
   request headers: {"x-forwarded-proto":"https","x-forwarded-host":"app.example.com"}  trustedProxies=[127.0.0.1/32]
   observed: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols  ->  ACCEPTED

== 10. untrusted proxy headers (rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders opt-in) ==
   config gateway.security: {"rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders":true}  trustedProxies=[]
   request headers: {"x-forwarded-for":"203.0.113.7"}
   [verify-client] proxy headers from untrusted address (remote=127.0.0.1)
   observed: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden  ->  REJECTED
   body: proxy headers from untrusted source

== 11. literal 'null' browser Origin (opaque context) does not bypass the gate ==
   request headers: {"origin":"null"}
   [verify-client] origin not allowed (origin missing or invalid)
   observed: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden  ->  REJECTED
   body: origin not allowed

SUMMARY: 11/11 scenarios observed at the expected HTTP status code.
```

### Focused tests and gates on head `1b5c1de`

- `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` — **8/8 passing** (trusted-proxy wiring regression, untrusted-peer reject, cross-site reject when opted in, **loopback cross-site allow by default** (v2026.4.15 regression guard), `Origin: null` reject, non-browser pass-through, IPv6 contradiction, IPv6 matching-across-forms).
- `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — **22/22 passing** (config-contract parity for new `gateway.security.*` fields).
- `tsgo` core typecheck: **clean (exit 0)**.
- `oxlint` on touched files: **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `oxfmt --check` on touched files: **clean**.
- `autoreview` (Codex, high reasoning): initially reported the `Origin: null` bypass; after the fix, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope / Out of scope

- **In scope:** `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts`), `src/gateway/forwarded-headers.ts` (validators), their tests, and the `gateway.security.*` config surface in `src/config/types.gateway.ts` + `src/config/zod-schema.ts`.
- **Out of scope (left to maintainer decision):** the `#98924` allowlist-wildcard contract, and the broader `gateway.browserOrigins` client/role-scoped policy direction.
- **`Sec-Fetch-Site` note for reviewers:** upstream deliberately avoids a blanket `cross-site` reject on MCP **HTTP** because browsers flag legit local MCP as cross-site. This PR mirrors that posture for the **WebSocket upgrade** path: the reject is **opt-in** (`gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests: true`) and runs *after* `checkBrowserOrigin`, so the existing origin allowlist / loopback-alias admission (shipped in v2026.4.15, PR #66665) remains authoritative. Native/CLI clients send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` header so they pass through regardless.

## Related

- Sibling enforcement: **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`, open) — which origins are allowed.
- Prior art (security findings this complements, addressed on main by earlier work): **#102834** (HTTP ingress CSRF under `auth.mode=none`), **#96486** (CSRF via the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, which this PR reuses verbatim rather than duplicating).
- Prior attempt by me: **#35109** (closed) — see "Prior Attempt & What Improved".

cc @steipete — this sits on the gateway origin/security boundary you own (and is the sibling of #98924 / #102834 and #96486, both addressed on main by earlier work). The `Sec-Fetch-Site` reject is scoped to the WS upgrade pre-handshake specifically because of the MCP-HTTP caveat you handled; happy to align flag names / gate position with #98924 before merge if you'd prefer.


---

## ClawSweeper Follow-up (head `1b5c1de`)

Addressed all four findings from the July 17 ClawSweeper review in a single follow-up commit (`1b5c1de7ed5`):

1. **[P1] Default-on Sec-Fetch-Site reject → opt-in.** `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` now defaults to `false` (`=== true` instead of `!== false`), matching this PR's stated "all flags default-off" design and preserving the v2026.4.15 / PR #66665 loopback-alias contract that browsers legitimately flag as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Regression test added (`allows legitimate loopback cross-site traffic by default`).
2. **[P1] Duplicate config field removed.** `gateway.security.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` is gone; `verify-client` now reads the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` so pre-handshake and post-handshake admission share one source of truth.
3. **[P2] Canonical IPv6 parsing.** `forwarded-headers.ts` now uses `normalizeIpAddress` from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` instead of `split(":")[0]`. Bracketed / unbracketed / port-suffixed IPv6 literals all normalize correctly. Regression tests added for IPv6 contradiction detection and matching-across-forms.
4. **[P2] Public config contract completed.** `gateway.security` plus its three leaf fields now have entries in `schema.labels.ts`, `schema.tags.ts`, and `schema.help.ts` (all ≥80 chars with operational guidance, per `schema.help.quality.test.ts`).

Net diff: +50/-40 prod LOC across 8 files. The PR got smaller, not larger. All unit tests (`verify-client`: 8/8, `schema.help.quality`: 22/22) and `tsgo` core typecheck are green on the new head.

target.title: fix(voice-call): unref ngrok startup timeout and mark closed on timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`startNgrokTunnel`'s 30s startup `setTimeout` was never `unref()`'d, so an abandoned tunnel promise kept the host process alive until the timer fired. On the timeout path the child was killed but `closed` was not set, leaving the `stop()` cleanup path inconsistent with the eventual `close` event.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unref()` the startup timer so it cannot pin the event loop, and mark the process `closed` on timeout so `stop()` does not try to re-kill an already-terminating child.

## User Impact

The voice-call tunnel startup no longer holds the process open when its caller has moved on; no change to successful tunnel startup.

## Evidence

- Regression test "unrefs the ngrok startup timeout so it cannot keep the host process alive": spies on `setTimeout` and asserts the returned timer's `unref()` is called. **Red before the fix** (`unref` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/tunnel.test.ts` → 16 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` is byte-identical for this region (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

target.title: fix(codex): skip runtime binding store when state API is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `@openclaw/codex` enabled, a typo like `openclaw stats --deep` previously printed `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'openSyncKeyedStore')` twice before the normal unknown-command diagnostic, making a healthy Gateway look broken. Root cause: during CLI plugin metadata discovery, Codex `register()` can run without a full runtime, yet full runtime registration (binding store open) ran on hosts that omit state.

Closes #107219.

## Summary

- Register the Codex CLI command descriptors up front so they surface in every load mode.
- Gate full runtime wiring (binding store, harness, providers, tools, event hooks) on the authoritative `api.registrationMode !== "full"` early-return, matching the `copilot` / `mxc` / `openshell` pattern — rather than sniffing for `runtime.state.openSyncKeyedStore`.
- Add regression coverage parametrized over `cli-metadata` / `discovery` / `tool-discovery` / `setup-only`, plus a full-mode assertion that CLI metadata is still registered before runtime wiring.

## Why registrationMode (addressing review)

Sniffing for the absence of `openSyncKeyedStore` silently converts *any* non-`full` host that lacks that method into CLI-only registration, which could drop the Codex provider/tools/harness/hooks on a malformed or future load path. `registrationMode` is the documented lifecycle discriminator (`cli-metadata` registers descriptors only; `full` owns durable state + runtime), so gating on it preserves the intended contract exactly.

## Evidence

`pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/index.test.ts` — **25 passed**.

Behavior proof driving the real `register()` entrypoint across load modes (empty runtime for non-full loads; durable `runtime.state` for full):

```
=== #107219 Codex register() behavior proof ===
-- metadata/discovery loads (empty runtime, pre-fix crashed here) --
mode=cli-metadata   threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1}
mode=discovery      threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1}
mode=tool-discovery threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1}
-- full load (durable runtime.state present) --
mode=full           threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1,"registerAgentHarness":1,"registerProvider":1,"registerMedia":1,"registerWebSearch":1,"registerMigration":1,"registerTool":1,"registerCommand":1,"on":3}
```

- Non-full loads: no `TypeError`, only CLI descriptors registered → unknown commands (`openclaw stats --deep`) now print just the normal diagnostic.
- Full load: descriptors **plus** harness, provider, media/web-search/migration providers, tools, command, and the three lifecycle hooks all wire as before.

## Did NOT change

- Full Codex registration path and everything it wires when `registrationMode === "full"`.
- CLI descriptor shape from `registerCodexCliMetadata`.

target.title: fix(zalouser): settle waitForExit when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `waitForExit` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`monitorZalouserProvider` registered an `abort` listener without checking whether the signal had already fired; per the AbortSignal spec, listeners added to an already-aborted signal never run, so `settleSuccess()` is never called and `waitForExit` never resolves. The fix adds a pre-aborted check before the listener registration, matching the pattern established in WhatsApp `connection-controller` (#109903) and QQBot `gateway-connection` (#109896). Risk note: proof uses the exported function with synthetic mocks; live Zalo API credentials were not used.

## User Impact

ZaloUser channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

**Before** (upstream `monitorZalouserProvider` on pre-aborted signal — `waitForExit` hangs):

Without the `abortSignal.aborted` check, a pre-aborted signal causes the `addEventListener("abort")` listener to never fire, leaving `waitForExit` unresolved.

**After** (same call with fix applied — resolves immediately):

The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before adding the listener and calls `onAbort()` synchronously when the signal is already aborted, resolving `waitForExit` and allowing clean shutdown.

**Focused tests:**

The existing `monitorZalouserProvider` tests in `extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.account-scope.test.ts` and `extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts` verify the monitor lifecycle continues to work with the fix applied.

**What was not tested:** Live Zalo gateway WebSocket session with production credentials; the fix follows the identical pre-aborted signal settlement pattern already proven effective in WhatsApp (#109903) and QQBot (#109896).

target.title: Bound QA runtime parity mock request reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA runtime-parity reads `${mockBaseUrl}/debug/requests` from a local mock server and previously used `response.json()` directly. That endpoint should return a small request snapshot array, but a broken mock server could return a large successful body and make the QA process buffer it before any validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the unbounded `response.json()` call with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper using a 256 KiB cap and a 30s idle timeout. The existing fail-closed behavior is preserved: non-OK, malformed, oversized, or stalled mock responses are caught by `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` and treated as missing mock tool-call data.

## User Impact

QA runtime-parity remains tolerant of unavailable or malformed mock debug data, but successful mock responses are now bounded before JSON parsing. Valid mock request arrays still resolve tool-call order normally.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 2 files.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts` (+16/-1): bounded response read with 256 KiB cap and 30s idle timeout.

Added runtime-parity tests in `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts` covering:

- non-OK `/debug/requests` returns no mock tool calls;

target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

target.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts:118` directly uses raw `fetch()` for MiniMax VLM API requests, bypassing the guarded fetch infrastructure used by every other network transport in `src/agents/`:

| File | Transport |
|------|-----------|
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + trusted env-proxy |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + env proxy eligible |
| `web-guarded-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (strict) |
| `tools-manager.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` |
| **`minimax-vlm.ts` (before)** | **raw `fetch()`** |

The raw `fetch()` path misses: SSRF protection (DNS pinning + hostname allowlist + private network blocking), redirect safety (loop detection, cross-origin header stripping, max redirect limit), debug capture (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED`), proper dispatcher lifecycle, and audit-context error classification.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is an architectural consistency fix. The previous revision of this PR added a bespoke `buildMiniMaxSsrFPolicy()` helper in `minimax-vlm.ts`. ClawSweeper [flagged](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106163#issuecomment-4956138257) that helper as a second source of truth for provider SSRF rules: it auto-trusted every non-default origin without the canonical metadata/link-local exclusions and did not honor `allowPrivateNetwork: true` for default hosts.

This update removes the bespoke helper and routes MiniMax VLM through the exported canonical provider SSRF-policy resolver (`resolveProviderTransportSsrFPolicy` in `provider-transport-fetch.ts`), so the image path uses exactly the same policy seam as every other provider request.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for default MiniMax endpoints. The MiniMax VLM image understanding path (`MiniMax-VL-01`) continues to work identically. The fix is transparent: same URL, same headers, same body — just routed through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode` (matching `provider-transport-fetch.ts`).

**Custom endpoint compatibility**: Operators using `apiHost`, `MINIMAX_API_HOST`, or `modelBaseUrl` to point at private/local MiniMax-compatible endpoints continue to work — the configured origin is preserved via the canonical resolver's `trustConfiguredBaseUrlOrigin` semantics, with the same metadata/link-local exclusions as other provider transports. An explicit `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` now grants broad private-network access for trusted default-host private-DNS setups, matching the provider transport contract.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests

- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts`: **21/21** ✅
- `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`: **32/32** ✅
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`: **93/93** ✅

Commands run:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/image.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts
```

### SSRF Policy Design (ClawSweeper P1 Resolution)

MiniMax VLM now calls `resolveProviderTransportSsrFPolicy({ baseUrl: host, url, allowPrivateNetwork, trustConfiguredBaseUrlOrigin: true })`, reusing the canonical resolver from `provider-transport-fetch.ts`:

- **All hosts** get `hostnameAllowlist` for DNS rebinding protection.
- **Trusted configured origins** (operator-set `apiHost` / `MINIMAX_API_HOST` / `modelBaseUrl`) get `allowedOrigins`, with the same metadata/link-local exclusions (`metadata.*`, link-local IPs, cloud-metadata IPs) as other provider transports.
- **`allowPrivateNetwork: true`** adds the broad private-network flag, matching the provider transport contract.
- **`allowPrivateNetwork: false`** withholds the broad private-network flag while keeping the configured origin pinned.

Tests verify the scenarios ClawSweeper requested:

1. **Default host** (`api.minimax.io`) → `hostnameAllowlist` + `allowedOrigins` pinned to the default origin, no private-network flags.
2. **Custom public host** (`custom-minimax.example.com`) → `hostnameAllowlist` + `allowedOrigins`, no private-network flags.
3. **Loopback host** (`localhost:8080`) → `hostnameAllowlist` + `allowedOrigins` (operator-configured local endpoint).
4. **`allowPrivateNetwork: true` on a custom host** → `allowedOrigins` + `allowPrivateNetwork: true`.
5. **`allowPrivateNetwork: false`** → configured origin remains pinned, no broad private-network flag.
6. **Metadata-like origin** (`metadata.minimax.local`) → no policy produced; guarded fetch defaults apply.
7. **Link-local origin** (`169.254.1.1`) → no policy produced; guarded fetch defaults apply.

### Lint / Types

- `oxlint`: ✅
- `oxfmt --check`: ✅
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json`: ✅
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`: ✅

### Live Behavior Proof

The previous live proof (local MiniMax-compatible forwarding endpoint on `http://127.0.0.1:18990`) still applies: the request path continues to go through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode`. The only change is the SSRF policy is now produced by the canonical resolver instead of a MiniMax-specific helper, so the custom-origin path still works and the default-host path now honors the standard provider `allowPrivateNetwork` semantics.

### Changes

- Replace raw `fetch()` with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode`.
- Remove the bespoke `buildMiniMaxSsrFPolicy()` helper.
- Use `resolveProviderTransportSsrFPolicy()` from `provider-transport-fetch.ts` for the SSRF policy.
- Update `src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts` to assert canonical policy behavior, including metadata/link-local exclusions and explicit `allowPrivateNetwork` true/false.
- Fix `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` mock setup so tests that fall back to the generic image runtime continue to intercept `global.fetch`, and tests that route through the MiniMax provider registry intercept `minimaxUnderstandImage`.

Fixes #106163

target.title: improve: let Code Mode use declared tool result shapes
target.body:
Related: #109288
Follow-up to #109651 and #109290

AI-assisted: Yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode learned exact tool ids and compact input signatures from #109651, but every tool result still appeared as unknown. Even when a tool had a stable structured result, models often spent one exec returning the raw value and another exec processing fields they could have known up front. This left avoidable model turns, tokens, and latency in common multi-operation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trusted OpenClaw core and plugin tools can now declare an optional `outputSchema` for `AgentToolResult.details`. Code Mode and Tool Search expose a bounded TypeScript-style output hint only when that schema is complete and closed; open, oversized, unsupported, MCP, and client schemas remain unknown and raw-first.

OpenClaw compiles trusted output schemas before execution, then validates final details after normal hooks. The embedded executor converts accepted results into deep-frozen JSON snapshots before queuing transcript projections, validates that exact snapshot, and returns it for a second host-boundary acceptance pass; rejected or later-mutated values therefore cannot enter session history as successful hidden-tool results. Framework-owned pre-execution policy blocks remain outside the success schema and are recognized by object identity, so calls reject with the denial reason before generated code can treat a block as a successful value; tool-authored blocked lookalikes still fail validation. Runtime/provider normalization preserves the result contract when it clones tool definitions. The compact renderer has strict depth/property/character/union bounds and normalizes AJV-style nullable schemas so every validator-accepted `null` remains visible to generated code. Remote and client schemas stay deferred as `input: "unknown"` and use object identity for catalog reuse, preventing attacker-sized metadata walks while preserving schema-replacement invalidation. `agents_list` adopts the contract as the first built-in example.

The change also promotes Code Mode to a dedicated `/tools/code-mode` documentation page with Quickstart, runtime semantics, guest API, output-contract authoring, trust/validation rules, fallback behavior, debugging, and validation guidance. The old `/reference/code-mode` route redirects to it.

## Maintainer Decision

Approve `outputSchema` as the supported optional plugin API for describing and validating `AgentToolResult.details` across Code Mode and Tool Search. Tools that omit it retain existing behavior. Opted-in tools get pre-execution schema compilation, final-details validation, and framework-owned policy-result preservation.

## User Impact

Code Mode can call and process tools with declared result shapes in the first exec instead of paying a raw-inspection round trip. Unknown outputs keep the safe existing raw-first behavior. Plugin authors get one documented result contract shared by Tool Search and Code Mode, without trusting remote MCP or client schema claims.

## Evidence

Live multi-provider matrix: four validated Code Mode tasks per provider over the real Agent runtime and a 72-tool catalog with adversarial decoys. Baseline is merged #109651; after is this branch.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Validated tasks | 11/12 | 12/12 | +1 |
| Model turns | 29 | 26 | -10% |
| Code Mode exec calls | 17 | 14 | -18% |
| Decoy calls | 0 | 0 | unchanged |
| Total latency | 81.4s | 70.4s | -13% |
| Input tokens | 38,827 | 36,025 | -7% |
| Output tokens | 2,388 | 2,380 | unchanged |

Stress: three complete Code Mode matrices produced 34/36 validated tasks, 78 turns, 42 exec calls, 57 underlying service calls, and zero decoy calls. Anthropic and Google were 12/12; OpenAI was 10/12. Both misses were the model filtering singular fixture value `plum` with the plural word `plums` after selecting the correct real tool, not a discovery, transport, schema, or decoy failure. A final OpenAI/Google pass kept every completed task at two turns and one exec. The final Anthropic retry hit provider overload before tokens or tools; earlier Anthropic stress was 12/12.

Validation:

- Exact final head: 275 focused tests passed across the live-bench parser, Code Mode, Tool Search, transcript projection ordering, runtime normalization, schema hints, `agents_list`, plugin SDK, descriptor cache, and optional tool metadata.
- Blacksmith Testbox: the final projection patch passed exact 4-file core/test typechecks, lint with zero warnings or errors, SDK API/boundary checks, import-cycle analysis, formatting, and architecture guards. An earlier branch-wide Testbox pass also completed 254 focused tests, all changed gates, and the full production build. Fresh hosted CI runs again before merge.
- Adversarial regressions cover malformed schemas before side effects, post-hook result validation, validation before transcript projection, immutable accepted-result snapshots, mutation after executor acceptance, policy-block rejection with preserved reason, blocked-lookalike rejection, nullable scalar/object contracts, cloned runtime tools retaining hints and validation, schema replacement, empty/oversized/intersected unions failing closed, closed/truncated/unsupported shapes, huge keys/catalogs, untrusted client/MCP schema deferral, and zero traversal of hostile schema proxies.
- Source-blind behavior contract: satisfied at 0.86 confidence; all seven clauses passed, including state-changing irrigation, missing-tool recovery, zero decoys, provider-error classification, and docs navigation/redirect behavior.
- Autoreview: clean on the final union fail-closed fix at 0.96 confidence, projection-order and immutable-snapshot fix at 0.92, runtime-normalization fix at 0.97, policy-block contract fix at 0.95, and nullable-contract fix at 0.94. Earlier review-driven fixes added pre-execution compilation, explicit completeness tracking, unsupported-shape rejection, bounded untrusted metadata handling, and the documented `input: "unknown"` sentinel.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`newSession()` and `resumeSession()` in the ACP bridge send the `session_info_update` notification via `sendSessionSnapshotUpdate` BEFORE returning the JSON-RPC result. Clients that key off `session_info_update` to learn the sessionId receive a notification referencing a sessionId they have not yet parsed from the result.

This causes Rabbit R1 sessions to hang indefinitely (rabbit-agent gates prompt delivery on receiving session_info_update after the result).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix defers the notification and subsequent `sendAvailableCommands` to fire asynchronously after the result is returned, using `setTimeout(..., 0)` to cross the response-write boundary. Both `newSession()` (line 394) and `resumeSession()` (line 554) are fixed. The full promise chain has a terminal `.catch()` handler.

## User Impact

Clients that expect session_info_update after the session/new or resume result now receive correct ordering. No change to the API contract, response shape, or notification content.

## Evidence

### Ordering tests (transport-level)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```
Two new tests verify that `session_info_update` is NOT called before the lifecycle handler resolves, and IS called after flushing timers — confirming result-before-notification ordering at the transport boundary.

### All ACP tests
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Typecheck
```
pnpm tsgo:core — EXIT: 0
```

### Fix pattern
Before: `await sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...)` → `return { sessionId, ... }`
After:  `return { sessionId, ... }` → `setTimeout(() => sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...).then(...).catch(...), 0)`

target.title: fix(ollama): models advertise tools when /api/show fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users discovering local Ollama models would still see tool support advertised when `/api/show` failed (HTTP error or network throw), so a broken or uninspectable model looked tool-capable in catalog/setup paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOllamaModelDefinition` treats missing `capabilities` as optimistic `supportsTools: true`. Failed `/api/show` previously returned `{}`, which left capabilities undefined. This change marks failed inspection with `showInspectionFailed`, keeping three states:

1. `capabilities` omitted (uninspected / successful show without field) → optimistic tools + name heuristics
2. `capabilities: string[]` (including `[]`) → authoritative show result
3. `showInspectionFailed` → tools conservative, reasoning name heuristics preserved

## User Impact

Local Ollama models whose `/api/show` fails no longer advertise tools, while reasoning-named models still keep the established name heuristic during transient inspection failures. A successful show that reports an empty capabilities list remains authoritatively non-tool and non-reasoning.

## Evidence

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | three-state unit matrix + HTTP 404/throw paths | pass |
| L2 | `buildOllamaProvider` enrich → definition on show fail | pass |
| L3 | Real `127.0.0.1` HTTP (`/api/tags` 200, `/api/show` 500) + undici `fetch` | pass |

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): guard provider catalog live URL parsing against malformed responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchLiveProviderModelRows` / `fetchLiveProviderModelIds` would crash with an uncaught `TypeError` when a provider model catalog API returns a genuinely malformed absolute URL in its `next` / `links.next` pagination field, or when the guarded fetch reports an unparseable redirect target (`finalUrl`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveLiveModelCatalogNextPage` and `fetchLiveProviderModelRows` each called `new URL()` on external API response data without try/catch. While relative URLs like `"?page=2"` always resolve safely, a malformed absolute URL (e.g. a hostname containing a space) throws `TypeError` and terminates model discovery. The fix introduces a `tryParseUrl` helper that returns `undefined` on parse failures, matching the defensive pattern already used by `withoutMatrixStateAfterSyncParam` in the Matrix transport (#109759). Malformed `next` links fall through to cursor-based pagination or `has_more` detection. An unparseable `finalUrl` triggers conservative cross-origin replay header sanitisation.

## User Impact

Provider live model discovery survives misbehaving catalog APIs without crashing; a malformed pagination URL is treated as "no next page" rather than an unrecoverable error.

## Evidence

**Before (upstream `resolveLiveModelCatalogNextPage` on malformed absolute next URL — `TypeError` crash):**

```
$ git stash push -m proof-before -- src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime.ts
$ node --import tsx tmp-catalog-proof.mjs
{"ok":false,"error":"Invalid URL","label":"before-fix"}
$ echo $?
1
```

**After (same harness with fix applied — graceful recovery):**

```
$ git stash pop
$ node --import tsx tmp-catalog-proof.mjs
{"ok":true,"result":["model-a"],"label":"after-fix"}
$ echo $?
0
```

The harness drives the real exported `fetchLiveProviderModelIds` with a mock fetch guard that returns `next: "http://exa mple.com/models?page=2"` (space in hostname).

**Focused tests:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-live-runtime.test.ts

```

New tests cover: malformed absolute `next` URL, malformed nested `links.next` URL, unparseable `finalUrl` (cross-origin replay header fallback), and malformed `next` with `has_more: true` (controlled incomplete-pagination error instead of TypeError crash).

**What was not tested:** Live provider catalog APIs returning malformed pagination URLs; the harness proves the defensive parsing guard on the real exported function with synthetic malformed input.

target.title: fix(memory): bound qmd taskkill cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD timeout, abort, and availability cleanup used synchronous `taskkill.exe` calls on Windows. A stalled system utility could block the Node event loop after the QMD operation had already reached its own deadline, delaying command settlement and gateway work indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows process-tree cleanup now launches `taskkill.exe` asynchronously and settles its cleanup attempt after five seconds without waiting for the utility to exit. The timed-out helper is terminated and detached, while the retained QMD child handle remains the final fallback.

The cleanup also rechecks the QMD child's authoritative `exitCode` and `signalCode` before forced escalation or direct kill. This avoids retrying a reusable PID after QMD exits while the asynchronous taskkill attempt is in flight. A timeout result is fixed before `kill()` runs so a synchronous child-process error cannot incorrectly trigger a second `/F` attempt.

## User Impact

On Windows, QMD operations now settle at their own timeout or abort deadline even if `taskkill.exe` stalls, so cleanup no longer blocks the gateway event loop. Normal graceful-to-forced tree cleanup remains intact for fast failures, and exited QMD processes are not targeted again by PID.

## Evidence

- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts` (27/27 passed)
- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` (2/2 passed)
- Regression coverage verifies heartbeat responsiveness during a stalled taskkill, five-second helper settlement, retained-handle fallback, synchronous kill errors, late taskkill events, and QMD exit before retry
- `oxfmt --check packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts`
- Targeted `oxlint` on both changed files
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Node 24 child-process source/types and Bun child-process compatibility were inspected for `spawn`, exit state, `kill`, and `unref` behavior

Proof gap: no Windows machine capable of deliberately stalling `taskkill.exe` was available in this session. The focused tests exercise the exact asynchronous OpenClaw path and event-loop behavior; GitHub CI remains the clean-environment gate.

target.title: fix(ci): bound npm resume GitHub lookups

## What Problem This Solves

The npm release resume identity check performs six sequential `gh` network reads. Each read currently uses synchronous child execution without a timeout, so one stalled GitHub CLI request can block release recovery until the surrounding 120-minute workflow job expires.

## Why This Change Was Made

The script now routes its default GitHub calls through a caller-owned runner with a 60-second timeout and `SIGKILL`. This keeps the release-specific latency budget local, preserves the existing 32 MiB output allowance, covers all six lookups, and continues to fail closed when a lookup cannot complete.

The runner accepts the same narrow child-process injection pattern used by sibling release scripts, allowing the exact production options and error propagation to be tested without a slow timer-based test.

## User Impact

target.title: fix: compaction usage guards and agent-loop turn correctness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cluster of agent-loop and compaction correctness bugs:

- A stream that dies before its terminal usage event persists all-zero usage; that anchors the context-size estimate near zero, threshold auto-compaction silently stops firing, and later requests die on context overflow.
- Tool results without `content` inject `undefined` into the transcript and crash provider conversion on the next request, aborting the run with a malformed message persisted.
- Compaction budgets skipped context-visible entries (plugin-injected messages, branch summaries), so the keep-recent window was computed against the wrong token totals and cut points could not land on those boundaries.
- Compaction could produce empty summary entries when there was nothing to summarize.
- A *successful* response with high token usage could be misclassified as silent overflow, popping the completed assistant message and burning the one-shot overflow-recovery flag.
- A threshold compaction that ran just before delivering a queued user prompt resumed the loop first, so the model answered the compaction summary unprompted.
- Follow-ups queued by handlers reacting to the run ending were never delivered.
- Mid-run system-prompt/tool/model changes did not apply to the next turn on the session path (the wrapper dropped the loop's per-turn refresh context). This is now an explicit `AgentOptions.prepareNextTurnWithContext` API (additive; baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow).
- `dispose()` left retry/compaction/branch-summary/bash/agent work running.
- Settings reload did not resync steering/follow-up queue modes; after-tool-call overrides dropped unknown result fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

These bugs compound in long sessions: broken usage accounting disables compaction exactly when it is most needed, and the loop-state gaps surface as duplicated or lost messages. The cut-point/turn-boundary logic is now expressed through one projection helper instead of parallel entry-type switches.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep compacting reliably; runs no longer crash on content-less tool results; queued messages are neither answered out of order nor dropped; mid-run model/prompt/tool changes take effect on the next turn; disposal is clean.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ai): guard stream error serialization against circular non-Error values (issues #106570 #106568)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI Completions and Google stream error handlers serialize non-Error exceptions with `JSON.stringify(error)`. When the error is a network error carrying circular socket references, `JSON.stringify` throws a `TypeError`, crashing the error handler and preventing the stream from closing gracefully — unhandled rejections, FD leaks, and hangs in downstream consumers during network outages.

This is the same crash at two sibling call sites (issues #106570 and #106568).

## Evidence

- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts:565` `error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)`
- `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts:469` identical line
- A circular non-Error (e.g. `{ code: "ECONNRESET", self }`) makes `JSON.stringify` throw, taking down the `catch` block that was supposed to emit the error.
- `scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs` reproduces it: OLD `JSON.stringify(circular)` throws; NEW guarded serialize returns `String(error)` without throwing.

## Fix

Wrap the non-Error branch in try/catch, falling back to `String(error)` on serialization failure. Applied identically at both call sites — one guard, same bug class, no new helper (the existing `src/utils/safe-json.ts` lives in the main `src` tree and is not importable from the `packages/ai` package boundary, so an inline guard avoids a cross-package export).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs
OLD JSON.stringify(circular) throws? true
NEW guarded serialize returns: "[object Object]"
NEW did not throw? true
RESULT: PASS — circular error no longer crashes the stream error handler
```

Closes #106570
See also #106568 (identical Google-provider crash, fixed by the same change)
## Runtime Proof

`scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs` mirrors the exact guarded serialization from
both call sites and runs a circular non-Error (network error with a self-reference):

```text
$ node scripts/proof-stream-error-serialize.mjs
OLD JSON.stringify(circular) throws? true
NEW guarded serialize returns: "[object Object]"
NEW did not throw? true

RESULT: PASS — circular error no longer crashes the stream error handler
```

The committed fix is also covered by the existing provider test setup where available;
the standalone script proves the guard without requiring live provider credentials.

## What Problem This Solves

`currentProviders()` in the session upstream-activity monitor read the **mutable** `getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry` to discover session-catalog providers. A standalone plugin load/reload swaps `activeRegistry` (via `setActivePluginRegistry` → `syncTrackedSurface(state.sessionExtension, …)`), so the long-lived background monitor could observe a post-swap registry with no catalogs and silently stop watching upstream activity.

This is the same drift class fixed upstream in `session-catalog.ts`, which now reads the bootstrap-pinned `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the pinned session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()?.sessionCatalogs`) instead of the mutable `activeRegistry`. The monitor is a persistent loop with no request-scoped pin, so it must use the stable surface the gateway already pins at startup.

## User Impact

The upstream-activity monitor keeps watching the correct session catalogs across plugin-registry churn instead of observing an empty set. No config or protocol change; no migration.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

QA runtime-parity reads `${mockBaseUrl}/debug/requests` from a local mock server and previously used `response.json()` directly. That endpoint should return a small request snapshot array, but a broken mock server could return a large successful body and make the QA process buffer it before any validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the unbounded `response.json()` call with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper using a 256 KiB cap and a 30s idle timeout. target.title: fix(bedrock): avoid replaying partial thinking signatures
target.body:
Closes #109881

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Amazon Bedrock Claude 4+ or newer models with extended thinking could persist a partial streamed thinking signature if the Bedrock Converse stream ended or failed before the reasoning content block completed. That partial signature could later be replayed and rejected by Bedrock as an invalid thinking signature, leaving the session unable to continue until reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock reasoning signature deltas are opaque and only safe to replay once the corresponding `contentBlockStop` arrives. The Bedrock stream runtime now stages signature deltas by content block index, clears the replay-visible signature while staging, and commits the staged signature only at `contentBlockStop`. It also strips transient streaming indexes from successful partial results so interrupted output cannot leak runtime-only bookkeeping into transcript content.

Existing invalid-thinking replay recovery remains responsible for sessions already poisoned by older output; this change prevents new Bedrock streams from persisting incomplete signature bytes in the first place.

## User Impact

Bedrock Claude sessions that hit an interrupted or failed thinking stream are less likely to poison future replay state. Completed thinking signatures are preserved byte-for-byte for normal Bedrock replay, while incomplete signatures are left blank and are not sent back as native signed reasoning.

## Evidence

Targeted regression test:

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Bedrock Converse reasoning signature deltas are no longer persisted into replay-visible thinking blocks until the matching `contentBlockStop` has arrived.

**Environment tested:** Linux source checkout, Node 24.16.0, local `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, patched `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts` imported directly through `node --import tsx`.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual patched `streamBedrock` production function with an interleaved Bedrock reasoning stream where block 0 receives a signature delta but never stops, while block 1 receives a signature delta and stops.

**Evidence after fix:** Command and output from the patched source path:

```text

import { streamBedrock } from './extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts';

    yield { contentBlockDelta: { contentBlockIndex: 1, delta: { reasoningContent: { signature: 'complete-second' } } } };

target.title: fix(feishu): honor abortSignal during app registration poll interval
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pollAppRegistration` in `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` accepts an `abortSignal` and checks it at the top of each poll iteration, but the interval sleep between polls runs on a bare timer. When the signal fires mid-interval, the loop keeps sleeping through the full remaining interval — which `slow_down` responses keep raising by 5s at a time — before the abort is noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The interval helper now sleeps via `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, the same abort-aware helper recently adopted for retry backoffs in sibling plugins (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). The abort rejection is swallowed inside the helper so the loop's existing top-of-iteration `aborted` check remains the single exit path and the `PollOutcome` contract (resolve with `{ status: "timeout" }`, never throw) stays unchanged.

Note: the only in-tree caller today (the `runScanToCreate` setup wizard) does not pass a signal. This change completes the function's existing public contract so the `abortSignal` parameter is honored everywhere it is already accepted — the bare interval sleep was the one remaining gap next to the loop's own `aborted` check.

## Changes

- Thread `abortSignal` into `sleepRegistrationPollInterval` at both call sites (transient-error path and normal path) and sleep via `sleepWithAbort`.
- Add a regression test: a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns `authorization_pending`, a 30s poll interval, and an abort fired 200ms in; asserts the poll resolves `{ status: "timeout" }` promptly and issues no second poll request.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel app registration polling (setup teardown, plugin lifecycle shutdown) now stop promptly instead of waiting out the remaining poll interval — which `slow_down` responses can raise well beyond the default 5s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c13e59662cbb538d7ff33eb100d2c26300b6f076`.

After-fix terminal proof — production `pollAppRegistration` driven outside Vitest (`node --import tsx`) against a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns `authorization_pending`, 30s poll interval, abort fired 200ms in:

- No change to the poll interval or the `slow_down` escalation policy.

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.
5. Confirm duplicate delivery does not cause concurrent duplicate dispatch.
6. Confirm the proactive reply targets the correct conversation/thread.

All logs and recordings must redact tenant IDs, user IDs, service URLs, tokens, credentials, IP addresses, and message content.

target.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics
target.body:
Fixes #95279

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Inbound user turns that OpenClaw decorates with model-facing metadata, plus the transcript readers that later render, replay, index, dedupe, or summarize those turns: Control UI chat text, CLI imported-session history, memory-host session corpus, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The root cause was a missing trusted source-of-truth contract for decorated inbound bodies: host-generated inbound metadata and user-authored text were stored in the same `content` string, so downstream consumers had to parse forgeable plaintext sentinels such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` or `Sender (untrusted metadata):`. Because the parser/normalizer could not distinguish host decoration from literal user text, metadata-shaped user text could be stripped or deduped incorrectly.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type metadata-looking text should not lose that text from chat history, imported-history dedupe, session logs, memory export, or historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix for a compatibility-sensitive session-state and data-format contract bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:** This PR adds an additive trusted inbound contract: persisted/runtime user messages can carry `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`, and inbound template context can carry `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`. Consumers prefer the trusted bare body when the marker is present, then fall back to legacy sentinel stripping for old unmarked transcripts.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source contract instead of adding another sentinel parser. The resolver treats `bareBody` as authoritative only when the trusted inbound marker is present, and the updated readers share that resolver so display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage logs all map decorated messages from the same non-forgeable contract rather than independently parsing user-controlled text.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The source of truth is the trusted inbound metadata on the message or inbound context, not sentinel text in `content`. Active-turn model prompts may still contain inbound metadata; historical display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage-log readers consume the trusted bare body when present.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Scope boundary: this PR only adds and consumes the trusted inbound bare-body contract. It does not change active-turn prompt construction, does not remove legacy stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not redesign plugin SDKs, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Existing unmarked transcripts keep their current legacy fallback. Marked transcripts get one trusted interpretation across the updated readers. The proof now includes focused regression tests plus an exact-head recorder-backed runtime proof that persists a decorated user turn through the shared transcript writer and reads it back through the real reader functions; external channel/gateway proof remains unavailable in this local environment and is disclosed below.
- **Risk labels considered:** `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** Consumers now trust `bareBody` only when `inboundDecorated === true` or `InboundDecorated === true`. A redaction hook that rewrites or mutates user `content` drops the prior trusted fields unless the hook explicitly supplies fresh trusted fields, preventing redacted content from being bypassed by stale bare-body metadata.
- **Why acceptable:** The contract is optional and backward-compatible. It narrows behavior by replacing text heuristics with a trusted marker while keeping legacy fallback for old rows. The test suite covers the reader paths most likely to drop or dedupe user-authored text.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Preserve literal inbound-metadata-looking user text through UI display/extraction, CLI import dedupe, memory-host export, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs when a decorated inbound turn carries a trusted bare body.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Old transcripts without the trusted marker still use `stripInboundMetadata()` and related legacy cleanup, so existing stored sessions remain readable and do not need migration.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment because the prework check reports no local gateway proof capability for the reviewer-requested live channel run. The submitted proof is current-head repository runtime proof plus regression proof over transcript/UI/CLI/runtime/memory/session-log boundaries using a real temp session transcript and synthetic message data; it now includes the hook-redaction boundary requested by review. Earlier broader checks also noted SonarLint was unavailable, `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a launcher sanity check, and a full non-incremental `tsc` run exhausted local Node heap; focused Vitest, tsgo, oxlint, diff checks, and the exact-head runtime proof listed below passed in the repaired worktree.

- **Environment:** Local Windows/Git Bash worktree, existing PR repair flow, repository Vitest runner, repository tsgo and oxlint runners from earlier repair rounds, and daily-fix verification bound to the current synced repair head `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `git diff --check`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`; `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with a recorder-backed exact-head proof importing `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. Earlier repair rounds also passed the focused trusted-inbound suite, core tsgo, core-test tsgo, oxlint shards, and a reader-only exact-head runtime proof after sync and conflict repair.
- **Key results / observations:** All current-head commands listed above exited 0. The session usage log regression proves both compatibility paths: an unmarked decorated legacy row strips injected metadata to `hello there`, while a marked decorated row preserves a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from trusted `bareBody`. The current-head recorder-backed proof ran on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`, used `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder` to persist decorated user turns through the shared transcript writer before reading them back, and observed: transcript writer persisted `inboundDecorated: true`; transcript writer persisted trusted `bareBody`; usage logs legacy row `hello there`; usage logs trusted row `"Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"`; memory corpus includes the trusted literal user text; memory corpus omits the decorated transport body; UI normalization returns the trusted literal body; an in-place `before_message_write` redaction clears the trusted marker; in-place redaction clears `bareBody`; usage logs show only `"[redacted in place by hook]"`; memory corpus omits the redacted bare body; UI normalization shows only the redacted row. RF-004 fixed by the redaction-boundary code change that compares post-hook content to the pre-hook content snapshot and clears trusted fields after any rewrite. RF-005 is a maintainer-decision item: this PR proposes the trusted inbound contract as top-level `inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody` fields, and maintainers should accept that shape or redirect it under an OpenClaw-owned metadata slot before merge. RF-006 fixed by the exact-head recorder-backed proof that covers trusted body and hook boundary in the shared session transcript writer path. RF-007 partially fixed and partially external: the redaction leak is fixed and proved locally, while durable field-shape acceptance remains maintainer-owned and contributor live setup proof remains unavailable here. RF-008 fixed by clearing trusted bodies after in-place hook rewrites. RF-009 fixed by the added in-place mutation regression in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`. RF-010 fixed by running `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` successfully. RF-011 fixed to the local runtime extent by the recorder-backed proof showing literal metadata-looking user text is preserved and redacted hook content cannot leak through trusted bare-body metadata. RF-012 was a non-blocking maintainer pass signal with no requested code change.
- **Regression guardrail:** Target test files: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` and `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`. The session transcript regression now covers a `before_message_write` hook that mutates `event.message.content` in place and verifies `bareBody`/`inboundDecorated` are cleared. The session usage log regression locks in both compatibility paths: one unmarked legacy decorated user row must still strip injected metadata, while one trusted decorated user row must preserve a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from `bareBody`. The broader focused test suite also covers transcript persistence and redaction, inbound context sanitization, CLI imported-history dedupe, UI extraction/normalization, memory-host session export, media-only inbound transcript expectations, and LLM-boundary historical replay.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings were reviewed. The resolver uses defensive message-like reads only at existing union/runtime boundaries where persisted rows, inbound template context, and UI-normalized messages do not share one static schema; those type escapes are guarded by explicit boolean/string checks and default to legacy behavior or `undefined`/`null`, not to silently trusting content. The session-files retry/catch is test-only Windows teardown cleanup and does not mask assertion failures. Default returns in the LLM-boundary and UI normalizer are narrow guards for absent trusted metadata. The larger diff is intentional because the contract must be written once and consumed at every affected display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log boundary; the latest merge-conflict resolution preserves current-main sender metadata under `__openclaw` while also preserving this PR's `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` fields.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local code paths covered by regression proof and current-head recorder-backed runtime proof. The only remaining caveats are the disclosed external live gateway/channel proof gap in this environment and maintainer acceptance of the durable field shape.

## Real behavior proof

- **Current-head redacted runtime transcript:** This PR now includes current-head real behavior proof on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`. The proof was run outside Vitest with `node --import tsx --input-type=module`; it imported `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, persisted decorated inbound user turns through the shared transcript writer, then read the generated transcript back through `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. It also persisted an in-place hook-redacted turn to prove stale trusted fields are cleared after hook mutation.

- **Boundary of this proof:** This is a local session recorder and reader runtime proof from the repaired worktree, not a live external gateway/channel proof. It avoids model/provider dispatch and does not require API credentials. The local environment could not provide the requested live gateway/channel proof capability, so that gap remains disclosed for maintainer or ClawSweeper judgment.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields on persisted/runtime user messages and inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body for decorated user turns while treating `before_message_write` as the redaction boundary.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): resolve abortPromise when stop signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a WhatsApp account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `WhatsAppConnectionController.waitForClose()` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller built `abortPromise` with an `abort` listener but, when the signal was already aborted at construction time, only called `stopDisconnectRetries()` and never settled `abortPromise`. `waitForClose()` races on that promise, so a pre-aborted stop signal could hang indefinitely. The fix resolves `abortPromise` immediately when `abortSignal.aborted` is already true, matching the existing pre-aborted handling for disconnect retries. Risk note: proof uses the exported controller with a synthetic open connection; live WhatsApp/Baileys sessions were not used.

## User Impact

WhatsApp channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

**Before (upstream constructor on pre-aborted signal — `waitForClose()` hangs):**

```
$ git stash push -m proof-before -- extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.ts
$ WA_LABEL=before-fix node --import tsx /tmp/whatsapp-abort-proof.mjs

{
  "label": "before-fix",
  "elapsedMs": 501,
  "resolved": false,
  "value": "timeout"
}
$ echo $?
1

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path. The same sanitization now also runs before the bundled Mantle plugin generates IAM bearer tokens via `@aws/bedrock-token-generator`, covering the last remaining Bedrock auth path that invokes the AWS SDK default credential chain. Valid static credentials remain unchanged.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, and inference-profile resolution. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.
- Sibling production-path tests now cover discovery and embedding client construction, in addition to streaming; valid static keys are preserved while blank bearer/static/session values are removed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` — 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts` — mantle credential sanitization tests pass; full mantle suite (3 files, 54 tests) and full bedrock suite (10 files, 175 tests) also pass.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files.
- `autoreview --mode local` initially found the SDK bearer-env gap; after the accepted fix, the required rerun reported no actionable findings (overall confidence 0.97).

AI-assisted. I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, and inference-profile control-plane paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.
