target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

Cyber:


target.title: fix(sandbox): cancel CDP probe response bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandbox browser startup could leave HTTP response streams open after CDP readiness probes. Both unsuccessful probes that continued the retry loop and successful probes that returned early left unread response bodies for garbage collection, which could retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForSandboxCdp` now cancels every probe response body before branching on the HTTP status. Successful probes, retry timing, auth headers, and startup timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser auto-start keeps the same readiness and failure semantics, while each completed CDP probe promptly releases its connection instead of leaving an unread stream open.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

I ran the same production-function harness from an `upstream/main` snapshot and this branch. The harness starts a real localhost `node:http` server, sends a streaming HTTP response through real Node fetch, calls the production `waitForSandboxCdp` loop, and observes the server-side TCP socket 250 ms after the function returns:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-before 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 503
```

The harness loads the probe loop from `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` (mirrored in `/tmp/sandbox-cdp-probe-*.ts` for import isolation). The server never ends its response body, making socket closure a direct observation of consumer cancellation rather than normal body completion.

Negative control / before (`upstream/main` at `e01027dd28a`), streaming HTTP 200:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":false}
```

After (`aac0533a40b`), streaming HTTP 200 and 503:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":503,"cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
```

The unchanged `cdpReachable` values are the behavioral controls: successful probes still succeed and unsuccessful probes still fail, while the real server observes prompt connection release in both paths.

Premise: Undici 8.5.0, installed by this repository, documents that every response body must be consumed or canceled because Node garbage collection does not release connection resources promptly. This probe only needs the response status, so cancellation is the bounded cleanup operation.

target.title: fix(mcp): doctor probes no longer start every server at once
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw mcp doctor --probe` would start a connection or stdio process for every configured MCP server at once. Large registries could therefore create an unbounded burst of external work during a single doctor run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor action now runs at most four per-server checks concurrently through the existing bounded task helper. Results remain sorted by server name, and unexpected check failures still propagate instead of being converted into successful doctor output. This is a focused operation bound; it adds no configuration or broader runtime refactor.

## User Impact

Operators can probe large MCP registries without `mcp doctor` launching every server simultaneously. All configured servers are still checked and reported in the same deterministic order.

## Scope and Competition Check

A fresh semantic open-PR scan on the pinned main snapshot found no equivalent fix. In particular, #103970 repairs legacy disabled-server migration in the top-level doctor/config flow, #108676 prevents disabled MCP servers from spawning, and #108104 isolates per-server runtime failures; none bounds the checks started by `openclaw mcp doctor --probe`.

The change is limited to doctor-action scheduling and regression coverage. It does not change MCP runtime defaults, configuration, public APIs, transport behavior, or ordinary agent MCP concurrency.

## Evidence

Regression proof before the production change:

```text
bounds concurrent MCP doctor server checks
expected 6 to be 4
```

Focused verification after the change:


Not covered: a live remote vendor MCP endpoint over HTTP/SSE. The near-real proof uses six actual local stdio MCP SDK servers so concurrency and child cleanup are deterministic without third-party credentials. The remaining risk is limited to scheduling: each existing per-server check is unchanged, and tests cover ordered results plus unexpected-error propagation.

target.title: fix(ui): explain replace-mode filtering in model picker
target.body:
Closes #104545

## What Problem This Solves

When `models.mode: "replace"` filters the model catalog, the Control UI showed the resulting models without explaining why other bundled or discovered models might be absent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured model-list responses now carry additive `catalogMode: "replace"` metadata. The chat model picker and Quick Settings use that metadata to explain that model settings are filtering the catalog, without claiming that every visible row was explicitly configured. target.title: fix(ai): preserve Unicode in provider error body truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider error bodies containing emoji or other multi-byte Unicode characters at the 4000-character truncation boundary would produce lone surrogate code units (mojibake) in user-visible error messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The error body truncation in `formatProviderError` used raw `String.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs. This replaces it with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which is already used by other modules in `packages/ai` (`tool-result-text.ts`, `mistral.ts`).

## User Impact

Provider error messages displayed to users will no longer contain garbled Unicode characters when the error body contains emoji at or near the truncation boundary.

## Evidence

### Tests (7 passed, 1 file)
```
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with JSON body
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with text body
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with no body
 ✓ preserves SDK message that already contains the body
 ✓ excludes surrogate pair cleanly at 4000-char boundary
 ✓ preserves emoji entirely within truncation limit
 ✓ does not truncate body shorter than limit
```

### Test Coverage
- **Straddling surrogate pair**: Places 🦞 (U+1F99E, 2 code units) straddling the 4000-char boundary. Asserts no lone high surrogate (0xD800–0xDBFF) remains before `... [truncated]` — the test that would have FAILED with raw `.slice()`.
- **Emoji within limit**: Places 🦞 at indices 3996–3997, verifies full emoji appears in truncated output.
- **Short body**: Body ≤ 4000 chars passes through without truncation marker.

### Mechanical Correctness
- `truncateUtf16Safe` is dependency-free and already used by sibling modules in `packages/ai/`
- No behavior change for ASCII-only error bodies

target.title: feat(gateway): add ticketed read-only MCP App host
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I understand the implementation and completed fresh autoreview passes with no accepted/actionable findings. No agent transcript is included because separate approval was not provided.

Closes #109851

## Summary

- Add a generic standalone MCP App host that exchanges a short-lived signed view ticket instead of exposing the operator Gateway bearer token.
- Keep the trusted shell on the Gateway origin and reuse the separate static sandbox listener; no view secret or dynamic app data enters the listener document.
- Keep the standalone host deliberately read-only and add one official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` fixture that drives both the existing authenticated Control UI host and the new standalone host over the real browser/transport path.

## What Problem This Solves

Future channel and standalone browser launches need to render one MCP App view without handing the page a reusable operator credential. The existing authenticated Control UI host is not a least-privilege launch boundary for an external browser surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process-local HMAC capability is bound to the current OpenClaw session key, MCP runtime session, view id, and view-lease deadline. The new HTTP boundary reconstructs only that live view, while the static host implements the stable MCP Apps initialization, ping, input/result, sizing, and teardown messages and rejects tool/resource requests.

This reuses the existing MCP runtime, view lease, sandbox proxy, and Gateway configuration. It adds no config/env surface, protocol version, channel launch UX, approval flow, or privileged capability.

## User Impact

When MCP Apps are already enabled, an authenticated Gateway client can obtain a standalone URL for the current view and open it without exposing the Gateway bearer token. Existing Control UI behavior is unchanged. There is no new default UI or channel action in this PR.

## Independent Landing and Backward Safety

- Existing `mcp.app.view` fields and semantics are preserved. `standaloneUrl` and its expiry are optional additions; ticket capacity, expiry races, or unexpected issuance failures omit those fields while returning the original successful view payload.
- The two new HTTP paths exist only behind the existing `mcp.apps.enabled` gate. Disabled installations and all other routes retain current behavior.
- The standalone URL is fully functional on this PR alone: initialize, ping, input/result delivery, read-only denials, reload, teardown, and rejection states require no later MCP Apps PR.
- The existing Control UI keeps its current app-only tool/resource authority. The conformance fixture proves shared/app-only tools and app resources remain available there while model-only tools remain denied.
- No current UI consumes the optional standalone field, and no current capability advertisement changes.

Exact dormant/additive boundary: the new route and optional Gateway response field are additive behind the existing MCP Apps gate. No launch button, channel integration, approval UI, tool/resource capability, or later-PR contract is advertised. A later PR may expose the already-working URL in channel UX, but is not required for any behavior enabled here.

## Evidence

- Real transport/browser path: an official self-contained `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.4` app ran through a real stdio MCP server, Gateway WebSocket authentication, Control UI Vite host, Gateway HTTP routes, static sandbox listener, and nested postMessage transports.
- Both hosts completed the stable `2026-01-26` initialize handshake and standard MCP `ping`, then received the original tool input and result.
- Control UI baseline: server tool/resource capabilities were advertised; the app-only companion tool and app resource succeeded; a model-only tool was denied.
- Standalone boundary: neither server tools nor server resources were advertised; tool and resource calls were denied; the only authorization header was `MCP-App v1...`, never `Bearer test`.
- Lifecycle: app-requested teardown removed the frame, reload reconstructed it, and a second load received the original result.
- Ticket security: unit/integration coverage rejects tampered, expired, wrong-session, wrong-runtime, wrong-view, replaced-view, and inappropriate reuse states; the browser scenario proves tampered and expired URLs fail.
- Origin/CSP review: the shell is static on the Gateway origin, the iframe is restricted to the exact separate sandbox origin, the listener stays static, the ticket remains in the URL fragment and is sent only in the dedicated authorization header, responses are no-store/no-referrer, and the shell never receives the Gateway token.
- Two final full-branch autoreviews after simplification/fixes reported no actionable findings. A reviewer-found missing standard `ping` response was fixed and exercised in both host modes before the clean final pass.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — full runtime and Control UI production build passed, including plugin SDK export and Control UI performance gates.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed with the frozen lockfile.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.test.ts ui/src/e2e/mcp-app-conformance.e2e.test.ts` — 13 gateway assertions and the complete Chromium conformance scenario passed.
- `git diff --check` and targeted `oxfmt` — passed.
- Repeated canonical-base updates were rebased without conflicts; every final `git range-diff` showed all three commits patch-identical. The push used a fresh `upstream/main` fetch and verified ancestry immediately before publication.
- Blacksmith Testbox passed the build and broad static gates before exposing two strict fixture type errors that were fixed. Two later Testbox leases failed during delegated file sync before executing code, so trusted-source exact-head fallback proof ran in isolated temporary clones with frozen dependencies.

## Simplification and Scope

The PR is six files: three production files plus two focused Gateway tests and one maintained browser fixture. Net production growth is 463 LOC. Most of that is the single standalone module owning the capability store, HTTP/security boundary, static shell, and minimal protocol bridge; keeping those concerns together avoids a new public abstraction or duplicated policy. The remaining production additions are narrow route and optional-response wiring. No cleanup, config, launch UI, or privileged capability is mixed in.

## Known Gaps

- This does not add channel launch UX, approval UI, or standalone tool/resource authority.
- Tickets are intentionally process-local and expire no later than the view lease; a Gateway restart invalidates them.
- At the bounded live-ticket capacity, existing view responses continue to work but omit a standalone URL until capacity expires.
- Required GitHub CI on the published head remains the final landing gate.

target.title: fix(onboarding): stop recommending tools setup cannot activate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the no-AI onboarding state told users to install Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, or Grok Build and then "check again", even though guided setup cannot turn those installations into a verified inference route. Pi and OpenCode are explicitly classified as unavailable whole-agent/ACP routes, Gemini CLI is excluded from the tool-free setup probe, and Kimi/Grok CLI installs have no guided detection path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recommendation catalog introduced in #109681 is shared by CLI, macOS, and Control UI, so correcting its inclusion policy fixes every surface at the source. The catalog now contains only Ollama and LM Studio (`appGuidedDiscovery`) plus Claude Code and Codex CLI (native setup candidates); the removed tools remain supported through their existing provider, OAuth, or ACP-specific flows.

Changing the empty-state wording would still steer users into a non-working check-again loop, while adding a second runtime filter would duplicate the detector's capability policy.

## User Impact

Fresh setup users now see four install suggestions that can lead directly to a setup candidate OpenClaw can test and persist. This does not remove Pi, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, or xAI support; it only stops presenting their standalone CLI installs as fixes for the guided inference empty state.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Empty-state recommendations no longer include tool installs that guided setup cannot activate or verify.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, commit `f14d2ea27eff` on branch `fix/setup-recommend-usable-routes`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-recommended-installs.mts` - imports the production catalog loader, prints the returned IDs, and rejects any of the five unusable setup recommendations.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  PASS ids=ollama,lmstudio,claude-code,codex-cli unusable=none
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All clients receive only the four setup-compatible install cards from `recommendedInstalls`.
- **What was not tested:** The external installers and provider login flows were not executed because this patch changes only presentation catalog eligibility; existing dedicated support paths are untouched.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       110 passed (110)

$ OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- scripts/lib/recommended-tool-installs.json src/plugins/recommended-tool-installs.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts
EXIT=0

$ git diff --check
EXIT=0
```

The catalog regression failed before the JSON change by returning all nine IDs. `check:changed` first attempted its normal Blacksmith Testbox delegation; the host lacked the `blacksmith` executable, so trusted-source validation followed the documented local fallback and passed conflict, ratchet, dependency, format, boundary, typecheck, core lint, and script lint gates.

Structured Codex autoreview was attempted with `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --stream-engine-output`, but the review transport returned HTTP 403 before a model response. The catalog producer, setup detector, all three client consumers, retained discovery contracts, removed tools' dedicated paths, and adjacent tests were reviewed manually.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - five misleading install cards are removed from the no-AI empty state.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config shape, persistence, default, or migration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - no installer, auth, network, or execution code changes.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - existing tool/provider support and plugin contracts remain unchanged.
- Highest-risk area: Narrowing a centrally curated product recommendation list could reduce discovery of tools that still work through separate advanced flows.
- Mitigation: Eligibility is limited to current guided-setup candidate contracts; dedicated Pi/OpenCode ACP and Gemini/Kimi/xAI provider paths remain available elsewhere.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: feat: align native macOS chat with the web chat capability set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat lags the web Control UI chat in day-to-day capabilities, even though much of the machinery already exists. Several fully implemented shared surfaces were unreachable on macOS: the sessions manager sheet (`ChatSessionsSheet`) was dead code with no trigger anywhere, assistant reasoning/tool traces were hard-disabled, talk mode / voice notes / per-message Listen were implemented in `OpenClawChatUI` and wired on iOS but never injected by the macOS host, and the mac transport silently dropped the `verboseLevel` session setting. The composer also lacked three everyday web-chat features: input history recall, reply/quote, and per-session draft retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligning the native macOS chat with the web chat's capability set, preferring host wiring of existing shared code over new surface area. Two staged commits:

**1. `feat(macos)` — host wiring (mac app + minimal shared passthroughs)**
- Sessions manager reachable: **Sessions…** toolbar action + Shift-Cmd-S opens the Active/Archived manager (gateway search, rename, pin, archive, restore). The unreachable `showSessions` state in `OpenClawChatView` is deleted.
- Assistant reasoning & tool activity visible in the full window, with a persisted toggle (`openclaw.webchat.showAssistantTrace`, default on; compact panel stays minimal).
- New `MacChatSurface` observing wrapper bridges live state into the once-constructed `NSHostingController` hierarchy: talk control (bridged to the existing `TalkModeController`/`AppStateStore` paths without touching the menu-bar overlay), voice-note recording (blocked while Talk Mode owns mic capture), per-message **Listen** via gateway `tts.speak` bound to the transport's server lease with local synthesis fallback (mirrors the iOS client), and starter prompts on empty sessions.
- `MacGatewayChatTransport` now forwards `verboseLevel` in `sessions.patch` instead of dropping it.

**2. `feat(clients)` — shared composer parity (macOS + iOS)**
- Input history: Up/Down recall of prior inputs (session-scoped, cap 100, transcript-seeded plus locally sent slash commands, draft stash/restore, Escape cancels), mirroring `ui/src/pages/chat/input-history.ts` semantics. Slash-panel navigation keeps priority.
- Reply/quote: context-menu Reply → cancellable composer chip → outgoing message prepends the exact web blockquote format from `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` (`prependReplyQuote`, same Markdown escape set, 500/120 UTF-16 truncation limits), so transcripts look identical across surfaces.
- Per-session drafts: composer text survives session switches (in-memory; revision-guarded so races with in-flight sends cannot eat newer text). Accepted tradeoffs vs web (no cross-launch persistence, no attachment drafts) are noted in code comments.

All shared-package API changes are additive with defaulted parameters; iOS call sites compile unchanged.

## User Impact

macOS chat gains: full session management (rename/archive/restore/search), visible reasoning and tool activity with a toggle, talk mode + voice notes + read-aloud in the chat surfaces, starter prompts, `/verbose` that actually sticks, Up/Down input history, reply-with-quote, and drafts that survive session switching. iOS inherits the composer features. Docs updated: `docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md`.

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawChatUI` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 48/48 XCTest; Swift Testing 853/856 with 3 pre-existing issues in untouched surfaces (see below)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --configuration release` — pass
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel` — 1280/1280 pass
- Gateway contracts verified in-repo: `tts.speak` (`src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts`), `sessions.patch` `verboseLevel` (`src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts:465`)
- Quote format verified against `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts` `prependReplyQuote` + escape regex
- Pre-existing OpenClawKitTests failures (not touched by this PR, reproduced identically on two independent checkouts including one with composer-only changes and one with host-only changes): stale pairing-copy expectations (`GatewayErrorsTests.swift:59`, copy changed in 551c9637d8a3), watch legacy payload decode (`WatchCommandsTests.swift:74`, compat added in ec65e10df7fc and lost by a later watch commit), and a load-flaky attachment timeout (passes 9/10 isolated). CI does not run this suite; follow-up task filed to repair it and add coverage.

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare both `canYield: true` and `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core validates both declarations; the scheduler sees the sequential identity before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. Only `canYield` tools remain model-visible and are excluded from Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs because those outer bridges cannot preserve the target tool's pre-execution scheduling identity. Existing non-yielding sequential tools retain their prior catalog behavior.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need migration; only tools that opt into yield declare the new capability and sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Add the explicit `canYield` tool capability and preserve it through tool-definition adapters.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Reject unsupported controls and controls from tools missing either required declaration.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.
- Keep only `canYield` tools on the direct execution surface; ordinary sequential tools remain catalog-eligible.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization, scheduling, compatibility, and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are applied only after finalization.
- Agent-core rejects yield from tools missing `canYield` or sequential execution before invoking the runtime handler.
- Agent-core proves a valid yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Adapter tests prove `canYield` survives AgentTool → ToolDefinition → AgentTool conversion.
- Catalog tests prove only `canYield` tools remain direct across Tool Search and Code Mode, while ordinary sequential tools stay cataloged; headless catalog behavior is covered too.
- Embedded orchestration proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- Scheduler TDD RED: run `29575710823` failed before the sequential guard existed.
- Scheduler TDD GREEN: run `29576120720` passed after the guard landed.
- Catalog scheduling TDD RED: run `29577281682`, job `87874669293`, failed before yield tools were kept direct.
- Compatibility TDD RED: run `29578570258`, job `87878675234`, failed when generic sequential tools still bypassed catalogs.
- Exact-head GREEN: run `29578965700` passed on `1dd9cf88a4deaab45ad92a081b760789955c1c46`: 55 successful jobs, 11 conditional skips, 0 failures, 0 pending.

- GitHub reports the PR `MERGEABLE`; `git diff --check` passes and the worktree is clean.

target.title: fix(workboard): dispatch after terminal cards retain claims
target.body:
Closes #108361

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Workboard card moved to `done` while retaining a stale claim would keep consuming its assigned agent's only dispatcher slot. Every later ready card for that agent could remain stranded even though the earlier card was already terminal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher now excludes terminal `done` cards from owner-capacity accounting while preserving the existing behavior for claimed review cards and genuinely running executions. A focused regression reproduces the stale-claim state through the real store and verifies that the next ready card starts.

## User Impact

Operators can move a card to done after a worker exits without the completion tool and still dispatch later cards assigned to the same agent. Active and review work continues to reserve the owner slot as before.

## Evidence

- `npx --yes oxfmt@latest --check extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.ts extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.test.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes oxlint@latest --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.ts extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

target.title: fix(discord): honor caller abortSignal during 429 retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`requestDiscord` in `extensions/discord/src/api.ts` retries 429 responses with a backoff driven by `retryAsync`. The caller's `options.signal` is honored by the fetch itself (merged into the per-attempt request signal), but the sleep between attempts used the default unabortable timer. With `retry_after` up to 60s (and `maxDelayMs` at 5 minutes), an aborted caller still waited out the full backoff and then issued one more request whose result would be discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryAsync` accepts a custom `sleep`; this passes `sleepWithAbort(ms, options?.signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` — the same abort-aware helper adopted for retry backoffs in sibling fixes (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). When the signal fires mid-backoff, the sleep's abort rejection propagates through `retryAsync` and rejects `requestDiscord` immediately, mirroring how an abort during the fetch itself surfaces. Without a signal, `sleepWithAbort` degenerates to a plain ref'd timer, so existing callers that pass no `signal` see zero behavior change.

## Changes

- Pass an abort-aware `sleep` to `retryAsync` in `requestDiscord`, wired to `options.signal`.
- Add a regression test: a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns 429 with `retry_after: 30`, an abort fired 200ms into the backoff; asserts the request rejects promptly with an abort error and the fetcher is called exactly once.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel Discord API work (plugin shutdown, gateway teardown, aborted operations) now stop promptly during 429 rate-limit backoffs instead of sleeping up to the full `retry_after`/cap and issuing a doomed extra request.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c6080c626be8c0b4bbfc286be079ea398ab9be5d`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

Same focused suite with the change stashed: the new test waits out two full 30s backoffs (`tests 63.72s`) and fails the promptness assertion. With the fix it rejects ~200ms after the abort fires.

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions test project reports no errors in discord files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- `timeoutMs` remains a per-attempt request timeout and intentionally does not bound backoff sleeps; the caller signal is the cancellation path.
- No change to retry counts, delay caps, or Retry-After honoring.

target.title: fix: avoid false stayed-stopped on launchd KeepAlive throttle
target.body:
Closes #109941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw gateway restart` on macOS would see a definitive false failure (`service stayed stopped and health checks never came up`) while a LaunchAgent-supervised gateway with `KeepAlive` was still inside launchd's normal `ThrottleInterval` respawn window and would become healthy seconds later. Automation that trusted that verdict could escalate against a recovering service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart health now prepares launchd KeepAlive supervision facts once before the poll loop and extends the continuous stopped-and-port-free early-exit threshold past the product `ThrottleInterval` when a loaded LaunchAgent is present. Unloaded, unmanaged, non-macOS, and non-KeepAlive paths keep the baseline fast-fail threshold. No new config knobs; supervisor facts are not rediscovered on every poll.

Compatibility: no config/API change; optional prepared `supervisor` param only. Performance: one `isLoaded` prepare at wait start. Usability: false failure verdict avoided during normal KeepAlive recovery. Security: no auth/trust change.

## User Impact

On macOS managed LaunchAgent installs, `openclaw gateway restart` no longer reports a hard "stayed stopped" failure solely because launchd is throttling a KeepAlive respawn. Genuine permanent stop / unload still fails within the existing overall restart health budget.

target.title: fix(gateway): force-discard ACP runtime after cancel/close timeout
target.body:
Closes #106631

## What Problem This Solves

When `/reset` or session deletion hits a stuck ACP cancel/close operation, the bounded gateway cleanup can time out while the cached runtime and its per-session actor lane remain reusable. A later turn can then queue behind the poisoned operation or reuse the same broken runtime, forcing an operator to restart the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now calls a manager-owned `forceDiscardSession` path after cancel or close timeout. The manager:

- retires the old per-session actor generation so fresh work gets an independent queue tail;
- detaches the cached runtime immediately and best-effort closes it without awaiting another possible hang;
- fences late cache/meta mutations and late turn events from the retired generation;
- clears only the retired generation's active-turn bookkeeping, so it cannot erase a replacement turn.

Normal successful cancel → close behavior is unchanged. This adds no config, protocol, persisted-data, or CLI surface.

## User Impact

An ACP-backed session can recover through reset/delete timeout cleanup without restarting the gateway or allowing the discarded operation to affect the fresh runtime.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping the QQBot gateway during or immediately after startup could leave `GatewayConnection.start()` pending forever when the caller AbortSignal was already aborted. The previous lifecycle also continued connecting after an early abort, which could leave a socket created during shutdown outside cleanup ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

`start()` registered abort listeners after work had already begun without normalizing an already-fired signal. The fix makes abort handling idempotent at registration, skips connection work for pre-aborted starts, and checks lifecycle ownership after each asynchronous startup stage. A socket created after an in-flight abort is closed before it can be adopted. Risk is limited to the QQBot connection startup and shutdown path; no config or protocol surface changes.

## User Impact

QQBot channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown overlaps startup, and startup does not retain a WebSocket that finishes opening after its lifecycle owner has stopped.

## Evidence

**Live configured-account proof (redacted):**

The patched lifecycle resolved in 146 ms after the real credential request and stopped before gateway URL/socket adoption. The already-running live Gateway was left online, and no messages were sent.

target.title: fix(config-cli,secrets): typed ExitError, JSON error output, and consistent stateDir for audit .env
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

### config get --json

`openclaw config get <path> --json` produces empty stdout when the config path does not exist. It only writes a text error message to stderr and exits with code 1. Automated consumers (scripts, CI) that pipe stdout expecting JSON receive nothing, making error handling unreliable.

### Secrets audit & apply .env path

The secrets audit and apply operations resolve the state directory for auth/model stores but re-resolve it for `.env`. If directory availability changes between calls (canonical `.openclaw` vs legacy `.clawdbot` directory appearing or disappearing), one operation can inspect or mutate two different state roots for the same run.

In `apply.ts` specifically, `projectPlanState` resolves `stateDir` once and uses it for config targets, auth stores, and legacy auth stores — but `scrubEnvFiles` calls `resolveStateDir` independently, so a root switch mid-operation can scrub a different `.env` and leave the intended plaintext credential untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

### config get --json

The `--json` flag implies machine-readable output on stdout. When a path is not found, the command now emits a structured JSON error on stdout, consistent with how `runConfigValidate` and `handleConfigMutationError` handle JSON-mode errors. The exit signal detection was also migrated from a fragile `__exit__:` string prefix match to the repository's typed `ExitError` contract.

### Secrets audit .env path

Reuse the already-resolved `stateDir` variable for constructing the `.env` path in `audit.ts`.

### Secrets apply .env path

Pass the `stateDir` already resolved by `projectPlanState` (line 296) into `scrubEnvFiles` instead of letting `scrubEnvFiles` call `resolveStateDir` again. This ensures auth stores (auth-profiles.json, auth.json) and `.env` are handled under the same state root for the entire apply operation.

## User Impact

- `openclaw config get nonexistent.path --json` now outputs `{"error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"}` to stdout (exit code 1)
- Non-JSON mode behavior is unchanged: error goes to stderr as before
- Secrets audit consistently reads `.env` from the same state directory as auth and model stores
- Secrets apply scrubs `.env` under the same state root as auth stores — no root-switch gap

## Evidence

### Real CLI proof — config get --json

**stdout:**
```
{
  "error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"
}
```
**stderr:** (build bootstrap logs only, no config command error output)
```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs config get nonexistent.path --json
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: dirty_watched_tree - dirty watched source tree).
...
```
**Exit code:** 1

### Real CLI proof — secrets audit

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR pnpm openclaw secrets audit --json
{
  "version": 1,
  "status": "findings",
  "filesScanned": [
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/.env",
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/openclaw.json"
  ],
  "summary": { "plaintextCount": 2, ... },
  "findings": [
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw.json", ... },
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw/.env", "jsonPath": "$env.OPENAI_API_KEY", ... }
  ]
}
```
Exit code: 0

### Real CLI proof — secrets apply (root-switch)

**Setup:** HOME contains both `.openclaw` (canonical) and `.clawdbot` (legacy) directories. Both have `.env` files with plaintext keys, plus `openclaw.json` with a plaintext `apiKey`.

**Before apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (canonical, SHOULD be scrubbed) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (legacy, must NOT be touched) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": "sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed"
```

**Command:**
```
$ HOME=$TMPHOME pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from plan.json
Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
```

**After apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (verify scrubbed) --
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (verify UNTOUCHED) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": {
  "source": "env",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
}
```

**Verification:**
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (plaintext key removed)
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=keep-me`
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (legacy key still present)
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=legacy-value`
- ✅ `openclaw.json` plaintext `apiKey` replaced with `SecretRef`

The plan targets `models.providers.openai.apiKey` with `scrubEnv: true`. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both directories exist, and the apply operation uses that single resolved `stateDir` for both auth stores and `.env` scrubbing. The legacy `.clawdbot/.env` is never touched.

### Tests

- `pnpm test src/secrets/apply.test.ts` — **31/31 passed** (includes new root-switch regression: "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores")
- `pnpm test src/secrets/audit.test.ts` — **26/26 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — **130/130 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts` — **5/5 passed**

### Lint & Format

- oxlint: clean (`src/secrets/apply.ts`, `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`)
- oxfmt: clean

### New regression test — apply root-switch

The test sets up a HOME where both `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot` exist. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both exist (it checks `.openclaw` first). The test:

1. Writes a `.env` with a plaintext secret in `.openclaw` (canonical)
2. Writes a different `.env` with a dummy secret in `.clawdbot` (legacy)
3. Runs `secrets apply` with `scrubEnv: true`
4. Asserts `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (secret removed)
5. Asserts `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (secret still present)

This proves one apply operation cannot switch roots mid-operation.

### Review findings addressed (revise round)

- **[P2] Reuse the operation's resolved state directory in apply** — `src/secrets/apply.ts:734`: `scrubEnvFiles` now accepts `stateDir` parameter and uses it instead of calling `resolveStateDir` again. Call site at line 341 passes the `stateDir` resolved on line 296.
- **[P1] Add root-switch regression** — `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`: New test "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores" proves the invariant.

### Behavior addressed

- CLI JSON errors now reliably reach stdout consumers
- Exit signal contract migrated from `__exit__:` string sentinel to typed `ExitError`
- Audit `.env` lookup uses resolved `stateDir` instead of re-resolving
- Apply `.env` scrubbing uses the same `stateDir` as auth stores — single-root invariant

### What was not tested

- macOS-specific `realpath` symlink behavior (Linux CI parity)

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

Tools that may yield must declare both `canYield: true` and `executionMode: "sequential"`. Agent-core validates both declarations; the scheduler sees the sequential identity before starting the batch, so a successful yield aborts the turn before later sibling tools run. Only `canYield` tools remain model-visible and are excluded from Tool Search, Code Mode, and headless catalogs because those outer bridges cannot preserve the target tool's pre-execution scheduling identity. Existing non-yielding sequential tools retain their prior catalog behavior.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need migration; only tools that opt into yield declare the new capability and sequential execution.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Add the explicit `canYield` tool capability and preserve it through tool-definition adapters.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Reject unsupported controls and controls from tools missing either required declaration.
- Stop a sequential batch after yield so later side-effectful sibling tools never start.
- Keep only `canYield` tools on the direct execution surface; ordinary sequential tools remain catalog-eligible.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization, scheduling, compatibility, and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are applied only after finalization.
- Agent-core rejects yield from tools missing `canYield` or sequential execution before invoking the runtime handler.
- Agent-core proves a valid yielding tool prevents a later side-effectful sibling from starting.
- Adapter tests prove `canYield` survives AgentTool → ToolDefinition → AgentTool conversion.
- Catalog tests prove only `canYield` tools remain direct across Tool Search and Code Mode, while ordinary sequential tools stay cataloged; headless catalog behavior is covered too.
- Embedded orchestration proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- Scheduler TDD RED: run `29575710823` failed before the sequential guard existed.
- Scheduler TDD GREEN: run `29576120720` passed after the guard landed.
- Catalog scheduling TDD RED: run `29577281682`, job `87874669293`, failed before yield tools were kept direct.
- Compatibility TDD RED: run `29578570258`, job `87878675234`, failed when generic sequential tools still bypassed catalogs.
- Exact-head GREEN: run `29578965700` passed on `1dd9cf88a4deaab45ad92a081b760789955c1c46`: 55 successful jobs, 11 conditional skips, 0 failures, 0 pending.
- `build-artifacts`, SDK declarations/surface checks, docs, lint/format, production types, test types, all selected Node shards, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and workflow sanity passed.
- GitHub reports the PR `MERGEABLE`; `git diff --check` passes and the worktree is clean.

## Notes

Prepared with AI assistance.

## Linked Issue

Closes #109761

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.
5. Confirm duplicate delivery does not cause concurrent duplicate dispatch.
6. Confirm the proactive reply targets the correct conversation/thread.

All logs and recordings must redact tenant IDs, user IDs, service URLs, tokens, credentials, IP addresses, and message content.

target.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw v7.1 Dashboard Returns 400 Error with llamacpp due to Missing Regex Anchors in Auto-Generated GBNF Schema
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw v7.1 Dashboard returns a 400 Bad Request error when interacting with a local llamacpp provider due to missing ^ and $ anchors in the auto-generated GBNF schema, while the exact same agent and model work perfectly through a standard Gateway message channel.

### Steps to reproduce

Configure OpenClaw v7.1 to use a local llamacpp provider (e.g., Qwen3.6-27B-UDiq3).
Open the native OpenClaw Web Dashboard and send a message that triggers a tool call or requires schema validation.
Observe that the request fails with a 400 error.
In the exact same session, send a message through a custom WebUI that uses the standard Gateway message routing (_send_to_gateway('main', text)).
Observe that the request succeeds with a 200 OK response.

### Expected behavior

In previous versions (and currently via the standard Gateway message channel), both the native Dashboard and external clients successfully communicate with the llamacpp provider without schema validation errors.

### Actual behavior

The native Dashboard fails with a 400 error. The attached gateway log shows the exact error at 18:21:55 UTC: 400 Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed: Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'. The llamacpp provider strictly rejects the malformed pattern, while the custom WebUI processes the request successfully.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

windows11

### Install method

_No response_

### Model

llamacpp/*

### Provider / routing chain

llamacpp with openai-completions

target.title: fix(ui): derive live cron and skill counts for Simple Automations card
target.body:
## Summary

The Quick Settings Automation card hardcoded cronJobCount and skillCount to 0, always displaying misleading zero counts regardless of real Gateway state. skillCount is now derived from config (same pattern as existing mcpServerCount), and cronJobCount is fetched once via gateway cron.status RPC on entry.

- Problem: Control UI Settings → Simple → Automations always showed "0 scheduled tasks" and "0 skills installed" even when the Gateway had real Cron jobs and Skills installed, because both values were hardcoded to 0.
- Solution: skillCount reads from config.skills.entries (config-driven, no RPC), cronJobCount fetches once via cron.status RPC when entering quick settings mode, with null-to-zero fallback until data arrives.
- What changed: `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` (+40/-3): added skillCount() helper, added cronJobCount state with one-shot loadCronStatus() RPC loader, wired counts into renderQuickConfig(). `ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts` (+37/0): added tests for non-zero counts and singular label rendering.
- What did NOT change: MCP server count (remains config-derived via mcpServerCount), polling behavior (no periodic cron.status calls), i18n keys, UI layout, channels/security/appearance quick settings.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #107852
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Operators opening Control UI → Settings → Simple → Automations always saw "0 scheduled tasks / 0 skills installed" regardless of real Gateway state, because cronJobCount and skillCount were hardcoded to 0 in renderQuickConfig(). This made healthy Cron and Skills installations look unconfigured and sent users to troubleshooting pages unnecessarily. The MCP server count already worked correctly by deriving from config — the same pattern should apply to the other two counters.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Control UI Simple Automations card hardcodes cron and skill counts to zero instead of deriving real values. Issue #107852.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (NewStartOS V4.4.2), Node v22.22.3, vitest jsdom environment, branch `fix/quick-automation-counters-107852`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts --run

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /media/vdc/githubode/openclaw-fixskills

 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts (37 tests) 2761ms
   ✓ renders the single-column settings sections with stable target ids
   ✓ changes the Control UI language from General settings
   ✓ drills into model settings from the Model row
   ✓ shows channel status and connect actions
   ✓ renders automation counts from props
   ✓ renders singular automation labels for count of 1
   ✓ renders Gateway host identity and resources
   ... (30 more tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
   Start at  11:25:16
   Duration  5.09s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.96s
```

```console
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 21ms on 2 files with 212 rules using 8 threads.
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Automation card renders "3 scheduled tasks / 5 skills installed / 2 MCP servers" when counts are non-zero (unit test verified).
2. Automation card renders "1 scheduled task / 1 skill installed / 1 MCP server" for singular counts (unit test verified).
3. skillCount is derived from config.skills.entries keys, following the same pattern as mcpServerCount.
4. cronJobCount is fetched once via cron.status RPC when quick settings mode is entered, with null-to-zero fallback until response arrives.
5. Counts reset to null on page/mode change and gateway reconnect, allowing retry on next entry.

**What was not tested**: A live Gateway + browser session showing the populated Automation card with real Cron and Skills data. The cron.status RPC path is unit-tested through the rendered output, but end-to-end verification against a running Gateway was not performed in this environment.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

In `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts:848-850`, the `renderQuickConfig()` method constructs the automation card state with literal zero values:

```typescript
automation: {
  cronJobCount: 0,
  skillCount: 0,
  mcpServerCount: mcpServerCount(configObject),
}
```

The MCP count works because `mcpServerCount` derives from `config.mcp.servers`. The Cron and Skills counts were never wired to any real data source.

Provenance: `carried forward by` commit 65e1232 (Control UI architecture refactor). The hardcoded zeros were introduced as placeholder values in the new Config-page layout.

Confidence: `clear`.

## Regression Test Plan

N/A — the fix is additive only. Existing tests continue to pass. New tests cover the previously uncovered behavior (non-zero counts rendering, singular labels). No config/API/shape changes.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

The Simple Automations card now displays the actual number of scheduled Cron tasks (from cron.status RPC) and installed Skills (from config.skills.entries) instead of always showing 0. On initial load before the RPC completes, the Cron count shows 0 briefly until the response arrives; the Skills count is immediately correct from config.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No (cron.status is an existing read-only Gateway RPC)
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Non-zero automation counts render correctly (3 scheduled tasks, 5 skills installed, 2 MCP servers); singular labels render correctly (1 scheduled task, 1 skill installed, 1 MCP server); skillCount() helper handles missing/malformed config gracefully; cronJobCount null state renders as 0; all 37 existing tests continue to pass.
- Edge cases checked: null/missing skills.entries config (returns 0), null cron.status response (falls back to 0), gateway disconnect before RPC completes (request id guard discards stale response).
- What you did NOT verify: Live Gateway + browser end-to-end flow; cron.status method-scope failure behavior (handled by null-to-zero fallback).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix follows the existing mcpServerCount pattern for skillCount (config-driven, synchronous, zero-RPC) and adds a minimal one-shot cron.status RPC for cronJobCount (no polling, no additional infrastructure).
- **Refactor needed**: No. The approach is minimal and does not introduce new abstractions.
- **Alternative considered**: Loading both inventories via skills.status + cron.list RPCs with polling — rejected because it adds unnecessary Gateway load, requires i18n changes for loading/unavailable states, and substantially increases the diff size (competing PR #108681 has +402 lines across 66 files). The skill count is statically available in config and does not need an RPC.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: The cronJobCount one-shot load fails silently on transient Gateway RPC errors, keeping the counter at 0 until the user navigates away and back. This is a known limitation.

**Mitigation**: The null default provides a 0 fallback (same as the current hardcoded behavior, so no regression). Retry occurs automatically on page/mode change (settings mode toggle, navigation to another tab and back, Gateway reconnect). The risk of permanent "stuck at 0" is low because most Gateway connections are stable, and the skillCount (config-driven) always works immediately.

**Compatibility impact**: None. No config, API, or migration changes. Existing behavior is preserved: MCP count unchanged, all quick settings layouts and i18n keys unchanged.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.title: fix(agents): strip trailing assistant messages after sessions_yield artifact removal
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109638.

After `sessions_yield`, `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` removes aborted assistant messages and yield interrupt custom messages, but leaves trailing regular assistant messages (from pre-yield tool work) intact. When a sub-agent completes and auto-announce tries to inject a continuation message, it fails because the last visible message is an assistant — causing a deadlock.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.ts`**: Added a second while-loop pass in `stripSessionsYieldArtifacts()` that strips any trailing regular assistant messages remaining after the yield-specific artifacts are removed. Updated `removeTrailingEntries` predicate to match.
- **`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`**: Added regression test verifying that after stripping a transcript with pre-yield tool work, the last message is a `tool_result` (not an assistant).

## Why this is safe

`stripSessionsYieldArtifacts` is only called inside the yield abort handler (after `waitForSessionsYieldAbortSettle`). It never runs on non-yield sessions. Trailing assistant messages in the yield context are always intermediate tool-calling work — not meaningful final responses.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: After sessions_yield, auto-announce continuation delivery fails with role-continuity error because trailing assistant messages block injection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.18.0, vitest

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts -t "trailing assistant" --reporter=verbose`

**Evidence after fix**: Test passes in both shards (agents-core 55ms, agents-embedded-agent 43ms). Last message after stripping is confirmed to be tool_result role.

**Observed result after fix**: 2 test files passed, 2 tests passed, 8 skipped (non-matching filter).

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end yield→announce flow (requires live sub-agent spawn + completion cycle, covered by integration environment).

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. The change uses one surrogate-safe helper for the 50-code-unit assistant bash preview, the 40-code-unit generic argument preview, and the shared sidebar truncation path used by persisted `bashExecution` records. It preserves the existing limits and ellipsis behavior while dropping a boundary surrogate half instead of emitting invalid text.

This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

Exported HTML transcripts now show stable compact tool labels when long commands or arguments contain emoji at a truncation boundary. Existing ASCII previews and their length limits remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(nostr): setup and DM targeting reject uppercase Bech32 keys
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users could not configure an all-uppercase NSEC private key or send to an all-uppercase NPUB target. Bech32 permits an encoding to be entirely lowercase or entirely uppercase, but OpenClaw rejected the uppercase form before `nostr-tools` could decode it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr key boundary now recognizes both canonical lowercase prefixes and valid all-uppercase prefixes, then continues to delegate checksum and mixed-case validation to `nostr-tools`. The lightweight setup entry and target shape detector follow the same rule; mixed-case Bech32 remains rejected.

## User Impact

Users can paste uppercase NSEC/NPUB values, including values copied from uppercase QR representations, into Nostr setup and DM targets without converting them to lowercase first.

## Evidence

- Regression red on `origin/main`: four focused assertions failed for uppercase NSEC parsing, uppercase NPUB normalization, setup validation, and target recognition.
- Focused green after the current-main rebase: `channel.outbound.test.ts`, `channel.setup.test.ts`, and `nostr-bus.test.ts` passed 28/28; the final review run added `session-route.test.ts` and passed 29/29.
- Affected Nostr suite: remaining focused groups passed 78/78 and 135/135 before the test-only control update; production code did not change afterward.
- The exact extensions test TypeScript config passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`.
- Formatting, `git diff --check`, targeted Oxlint, and Codex review passed on the six changed files.
- Live NIP-04 proof against `wss://relay.nostr.net` with randomly generated one-use keys:
  - control on `origin/main`: lowercase NSEC/NPUB published, was queried back from the relay, and decrypted successfully;
  - before: uppercase NSEC and NPUB were both rejected before publish;
  - after: uppercase NSEC and NPUB were accepted, and the encrypted DM published, was queried back, and decrypted successfully.
- The full changed-file gate is left to official CI because the local Node 22.22.0 runtime is below the repository's supported 22.22.3 floor.

target.title: fix: keep session thinking through transcript recovery
target.body:
Closes #109275

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with stored `/think` or `/verbose` session preferences could lose those preferences when command-session resolution rotates the OpenClaw session id for terminal transcript-registry recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps stored thinking and verbose preferences available when terminal transcript recovery creates a replacement session id but the configured daily/idle reset policy would otherwise still treat the session as current. It intentionally does not carry those preferences when terminal recovery overlaps a configured daily or idle reset boundary, so a configured clean-session reset still wins.

## User Impact

Users who set `/think high` or `/verbose full` keep that session preference through terminal transcript recovery instead of silently falling back to defaults. Operators who rely on daily or idle session resets still get a clean session without inherited thinking or verbose preferences.
